title.zh: 卷二十四 列傳第十四 王裕之 王鎮之 王韶之 王悅之 王准之
title.en: Volume 24 Biographies 14: Wang Yuzhi, Wang Zhenzhi, Wang Shaozhi, Wang Yuezhi, Wang Zhunzhi
title.raw: 卷二十四 列傳第十四 王裕之 王鎮之 王韶之 王悅之 王准之 Volume 24 Biographies 14: Wang Yuzhi, Wang Zhenzhi, Wang Shaozhi, Wang Yuezhi, Wang Zhunzhi

sentences.zh: 列傳第十四

translations.literal: Biographies 14
translations.idiomatic: Biographies 14

sentences.zh: 王裕之王鎮之王韶之王悅之王准之

translations.literal: Wang Yuzhi, Wang Zhenzhi, Wang Shaozhi, Wang Yuezhi, Wang Zhunzhi
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuzhi, Wang Zhenzhi, Wang Shaozhi, Wang Yuezhi, and Wang Zhunzhi

sentences.zh: 敬弘少有清尚，起家本國左常侍、衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: Jinghong from youth had pure and lofty tastes; he first took office as Left Attendant-in-Ordinary of his native principality and aide in the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Jinghong held himself to pure and lofty standards. He began his career as left attendant-in-ordinary of his native principality and as an aide in the guard army.

sentences.zh: 性恬靜，樂山水，求為天門太守。

translations.literal: His nature was tranquil and still; he delighted in mountains and waters, and requested appointment as Administrator of Tianmen.
translations.idiomatic: Quiet by nature, he loved mountains and rivers and asked to be made administrator of Tianmen commandery.

sentences.zh: 及之郡，妻弟荊州刺史桓玄遣信要令過己，敬弘至巴陵，謂人曰：「靈寶正當欲見其姊，我不能為桓氏贅婿。

translations.literal: When he reached the commandery, his wife's younger brother, the Inspector of Jingzhou Huan Xuan, sent a messenger summoning him to visit; Jinghong reached Baling and said to others, "Lingbao merely wants to see his elder sister. I cannot become a son-in-law living under the Huan clan."
translations.idiomatic: Once he took up the post, his wife's brother Huan Xuan, inspector of Jingzhou, sent word asking him to call. Jinghong reached Baling and told those around him: "Lingbao only wants to see his sister. I will not be kept as a dependent son-in-law of the Huans."

sentences.zh: 」乃遣別船送妻往江陵，彌年不迎。

translations.literal: Thereupon he sent his wife onward to Jiangling on a separate boat and for a full year did not go to receive her.
translations.idiomatic: He put his wife on another boat bound for Jiangling and did not go to fetch her for an entire year.

sentences.zh: 山郡無事，恣其遊適，意甚好之。

translations.literal: The mountain commandery had no business affairs; he gave free rein to wandering and roaming, and his mind greatly delighted in it.
translations.idiomatic: The mountain district had little official business, and he roamed as he pleased. He loved the life.

sentences.zh: 後為南平太守，去官，居作唐縣界。

translations.literal: Later he served as Administrator of Nanping, left office, and dwelt on the border of Zuotang county.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrator of Nanping, resigned, and lived on the edge of Zuotang county.

sentences.zh: 玄輔政及篡位，屢召不下。

translations.literal: When Xuan assisted in government and usurped the throne, he repeatedly summoned him, but Jinghong would not come down.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan held power and then seized the throne, he summoned Jinghong again and again, but Jinghong refused every call.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝以為車騎從事中郎、徐州中從事史、征西將軍道規諮議參軍。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song appointed him Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Chariots and Cavalry, Central Aide of Xuzhou, and Advisory Aide to General Who Conquers the West Daogui.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu of Song made him attendant-in-ordinary on the staff of the chariots-and-cavalry office, central aide of Xuzhou, and advisory aide to General Who Conquers the West Daogui.

sentences.zh: 時府主簿宗協亦有高趣，道規並以事外相期。

translations.literal: At the time the headquarters chief clerk Zong Xie also had lofty tastes; Daogui with both of them looked to matters outside official business.
translations.idiomatic: Daogui's chief clerk Zong Xie shared his high-minded tastes, and the two men looked to Daogui for companionship beyond the duties of office.

sentences.zh: 嘗共酣飲，敬弘因醉失禮，為外司所白，道規即更引還，重申初燕。

translations.literal: Once they drank together to intoxication; Jinghong through drunkenness lost propriety and was reported by the external office; Daogui immediately summoned him back again and renewed the first feast.
translations.idiomatic: They once drank together until Jinghong, drunk, breached etiquette. An outside office reported him, but Daogui immediately had him brought back and held the first banquet again.

sentences.zh: 永初中，累遷吏部尚書，敬弘每被召，即便祗奉，既到宜退，旋復解官。

translations.literal: In the beginning of the Yongchu era he was repeatedly promoted to Director of the Ministry of Personnel; each time Jinghong was summoned he at once reverently accepted, but once he arrived he ought to withdraw, and presently he again resigned office.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Yongchu period he rose repeatedly to director of the Ministry of Personnel. Each summons Jinghong accepted at once, but as soon as he took up the post he resigned again.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉其志，不苟違也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised his resolve and did not lightly go against it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired his resolve and did not press him against his will.

sentences.zh: 除廬陵王師，加散騎常侍。

translations.literal: He was appointed Tutor to the Prince of Luling, with additional rank as Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He was named tutor to the Prince of Luling and given the additional title of supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 自陳無德，不可師範令王，固讓不拜。

translations.literal: He declared himself without virtue and unable to be a model for a prince, firmly declined, and did not accept the appointment.
translations.idiomatic: He protested that he lacked the virtue to instruct a prince, refused firmly, and would not take the appointment.

sentences.zh: 元嘉三年，為尚書僕射，關署文案，初不省讀。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yuanjia he served as Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; he handled documents at the gate offices but from the first did not examine and read them.
translations.idiomatic: In Yuanjia year 3 he became vice director of the Masters of Writing. Papers passed through his office, but he never read them.

sentences.zh: 嘗豫聽訟，上問疑獄，敬弘不對。

translations.literal: Once he participated in hearing lawsuits; the emperor asked about doubtful cases, and Jinghong did not reply.
translations.idiomatic: Once, while sitting in on a trial, the emperor asked about a difficult case. Jinghong said nothing.

sentences.zh: 上變色問左右：「何故不以訊牒副僕射？

translations.literal: The emperor changed color and asked those beside him, "Why were the interrogation documents not given to the Vice Director?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's face darkened. He asked his attendants: "Why were the case files not given to the vice director?"

sentences.zh: 」敬弘曰：「臣乃得訊牒讀之，正自不解。

translations.literal: Jinghong said, "It is only because I received the interrogation documents and read them that I know I truly do not understand."
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong said: "I did receive the files and read them. That is precisely why I know I cannot answer."

sentences.zh: 」上甚不悅。

translations.literal: The emperor was very displeased.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was deeply displeased.

sentences.zh: 雖加禮敬，亦不以時務及之。

translations.literal: Although additional ritual respect was shown him, state affairs were also not entrusted to him in timely fashion.
translations.idiomatic: Courtesy toward him increased, but he was never drawn into the business of government.

sentences.zh: 六年，遷尚書令，固讓，表求還東。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing; he firmly declined and memorialized requesting return to the east.
translations.idiomatic: In year 6 he was promoted to director of the Masters of Writing. He refused and petitioned to return east.

sentences.zh: 上不能奪。

translations.literal: The emperor could not override him.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor could not make him stay.

sentences.zh: 改授侍中、特進、左光祿大夫，給親信三十人。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Special Courtier, Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall, with thirty personal attendants granted.
translations.idiomatic: Instead he was made attendant-in-ordinary, special courtier, and left grand master of the bright hall, with thirty personal attendants.

sentences.zh: 及東歸，車駕幸冶亭餞送。

translations.literal: When he returned east, the imperial carriage went to Ye Pavilion to see him off with a farewell feast.
translations.idiomatic: When he went home east, the emperor himself came to Ye Pavilion to see him off.

sentences.zh: 十二年，徵為太子少傅，敬弘詣都上表固辭不拜，東歸，上時不豫，自力見焉。

translations.literal: In the twelfth year he was summoned as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent; Jinghong went to the capital and memorialized firmly declining and not accepting appointment, then returned east; the emperor was then unwell, and Jinghong exerted himself to go see him.
translations.idiomatic: In year 12 he was summoned to be junior tutor to the heir apparent. Jinghong went to court, petitioned to decline, and went home again. The emperor was ill at the time, and Jinghong forced himself to visit him.

sentences.zh: 十六年，以為左光祿大夫、開府儀同三司，侍中如故。

translations.literal: In the sixteenth year he was appointed Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall and Grand Master with Golden Tally Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies, Attendant-in-Ordinary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In year 16 he was named left grand master of the bright hall and grand master with golden tally equal in ceremony to the three excellencies, retaining his post as attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 又詣都表辭，竟不拜東歸。

translations.literal: Again he went to the capital and memorialized a decline, and in the end did not accept appointment and returned east.
translations.idiomatic: He went to the capital once more, declined again in a memorial, and never took the appointment.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，復申前命，復辭。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year the former appointment was renewed; he again declined.
translations.idiomatic: In year 23 the same appointment was offered again. He refused once more.

sentences.zh: 明年，薨于余杭之舍亭山，年八十八。

translations.literal: The next year he died at Sheting Mountain in Yuhang, aged eighty-eight.
translations.idiomatic: The following year he died at Sheting Mountain in Yuhang, aged eighty-eight.

sentences.zh: 順帝升明三年，追諡文貞公。

translations.literal: In the third year of Shengming under Emperor Shun, he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke Wen Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In Shengming year 3 under Emperor Shun he was posthumously enfeoffed as Duke Wen Zhen.

sentences.zh: 敬弘形狀短而起坐端方，桓玄謂之「彈棋發八勢」。

translations.literal: Jinghong's form was short, yet in rising and sitting he was upright and square; Huan Xuan called him "the eight formations of flicking chess pieces."
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong was short in stature but sat and stood with perfect composure. Huan Xuan nicknamed him "the eight formations of flicking chess stones."

sentences.zh: 所居舍亭山，林澗環周，備登臨之美，故時人謂之王東山。

translations.literal: The Sheting Mountain where he dwelt had forests and streams all around, fully possessing the beauty of climbing and viewing; therefore people of the time called him Wang of the Eastern Mountain.
translations.idiomatic: His home at Sheting Mountain was ringed with forest and stream, ideal for climbing and looking out. People called him Wang of the Eastern Mountain.

sentences.zh: 文帝嘗問為政得失，對曰：「天下有道，庶人不議。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen once asked about the gains and losses of governing; he replied, "When all under Heaven has the Way, common people do not discuss it."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen once asked him about the strengths and failings of government. He answered: "When the realm is well governed, ordinary people have nothing to debate."

sentences.zh: 」上高其言。

translations.literal: The emperor held his words in high esteem.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor admired the reply.

sentences.zh: 左右嘗使二老婦女，戴五條辮，著青紋絝袼，飾以朱粉。

translations.literal: Those beside him once made two old women wear five-strand braids, blue-patterned trousers and sleeves, adorned with cinnabar powder.
translations.idiomatic: His attendants once dressed two elderly women in five-strand braids, blue-patterned trousers and sleeves, and cinnabar makeup.

sentences.zh: 女適尚書僕射何尚之弟述之。

translations.literal: His daughter married the younger brother of Vice Director of the Masters of Writing He Shangzhi, Shuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His daughter married Shuzhi, younger brother of Vice Director He Shangzhi.

sentences.zh: 敬弘嘗往何氏看女，遇尚之不在，因寄齋中臥。

translations.literal: Jinghong once went to the He household to see his daughter; he encountered Shangzhi not at home and therefore lodged to sleep in the fasting hall.
translations.idiomatic: Once, visiting his daughter at the He house, he found Shangzhi away and slept in the guest hall.

sentences.zh: 俄頃尚之還，敬弘使二婦女守合，不聽尚之入，云：「正熱不堪相見，君可且去」。

translations.literal: Before long Shangzhi returned; Jinghong had the two women guard the door and would not allow Shangzhi to enter, saying, "It is truly too hot to bear meeting; you may for the moment go."
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi soon returned. Jinghong had the two women block the door and would not let him in. "It's unbearably hot," he said. "You'd better leave for now."

sentences.zh: 尚之於是移於他室。

translations.literal: Shangzhi thereupon moved to another room.
translations.idiomatic: Shangzhi moved to another room.

sentences.zh: 上將為廬陵王納其女，辭曰：「臣女幼，既許孔淳之息。

translations.literal: The emperor was about to take his daughter in marriage for the Prince of Luling; he declined, saying, "My daughter is young; she has already been promised to the son of Kong Chunzhi."
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor wished to marry his daughter to the Prince of Luling, he declined: "My daughter is still young, and I have already promised her to Kong Chunzhi's son."

sentences.zh: 」子恢之被召為秘書郎，敬弘為求奉朝請，與恢之書曰：「彼秘書有限故有競，朝請無限故無競，吾欲使汝處不競之地。

translations.literal: When his son Huizhi was summoned as Secretary Gentleman, Jinghong requested for him the post of Attendant at Court Audience, and wrote to Huizhi, saying, "That secretary post is limited, therefore there is competition; court audience is unlimited, therefore there is no competition. I wish to place you in a place without competition."
translations.idiomatic: When his son Huizhi was called up as secretary gentleman, Jinghong asked instead for the post of attendant at court audience and wrote to him: "The secretariat has limited seats, so men compete for them. Court audience has no limit, so there is no rivalry. I want you where no one has to fight."

sentences.zh: 」文帝嘉之，並見許。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen praised this, and both requests were granted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen approved, and both requests were granted.

sentences.zh: 敬弘見兒孫，歲中不過一再相見，見輒克日。

translations.literal: When Jinghong saw his sons and grandsons, within the year he did not exceed one or two meetings; when he met them he fixed the day.
translations.idiomatic: He saw his sons and grandsons at most once or twice a year, and even then only on a day he had set in advance.

sentences.zh: 未嘗教子孫學問，各隨所欲。

translations.literal: He never taught his sons and grandsons learning; each followed his own desire.
translations.idiomatic: He never drilled his descendants in scholarship. Each was left to his own inclinations.

sentences.zh: 人或問之，答曰：「丹朱不應乏教，甯越不聞被捶。

translations.literal: When someone asked him about this, he replied, "Danzhu surely did not lack instruction; Ning Yue never heard of being beaten."
translations.idiomatic: Asked why, he said: "Danzhu cannot have lacked teachers, yet Ning Yue never needed the rod."

sentences.zh: 」恢之位新安太守，嘗請假定省。

translations.literal: Huizhi held the post of Administrator of Xin'an and once requested temporary leave to visit home.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi, then administrator of Xin'an, once asked leave to visit home.

sentences.zh: 敬弘克日見之，至日輒不果。

translations.literal: Jinghong fixed a day to see him; when the day arrived he still did not succeed in meeting.
translations.idiomatic: Jinghong named a day to receive him. When the day came, he still would not see him.

sentences.zh: 假日將盡，恢之求辭，敬弘呼前至合，復不見。

translations.literal: When the leave was nearly ended, Huizhi asked to take leave; Jinghong summoned him forward to the door, yet again did not see him.
translations.idiomatic: As the leave was ending Huizhi came to bid farewell. Jinghong called him to the door and again refused to meet him.

sentences.zh: 恢之於合外拜辭流涕而去。

translations.literal: Outside the door Huizhi bowed in leave with tears streaming and departed.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi bowed outside the door in tears and left.

sentences.zh: 恢之弟瓚之，位吏部尚書、金紫光祿大夫，諡貞子。

translations.literal: Huizhi's younger brother Zanzhi held the posts of Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel, posthumous title Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: Huizhi's brother Zanzhi became director of the Ministry of Personnel and grand master of the bright hall with golden tassel. He was posthumously titled Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 瓚之弟升之，位都官尚書。

translations.literal: Zanzhi's younger brother Shengshi held the post of Director of the Ministry of Punishments.
translations.idiomatic: Zanzhi's brother Shengzhi served as director of the Ministry of Punishments.

sentences.zh: 瓚之子秀之。

translations.literal: Zanzhi's son was Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Xiuzhi.

sentences.zh: 秀之字伯奮，幼時，祖父敬弘愛其風采。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi, styled Bofen, in childhood his grandfather Jinghong loved his bearing and mien.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi, styled Bofen, was admired from boyhood by his grandfather Jinghong for his bearing.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為太子舍人。

translations.literal: He served Song as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he served as attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 父卒，廬於墓側，服闋，復職。

translations.literal: When his father died he built a hut beside the tomb; when mourning ended he resumed office.
translations.idiomatic: When his father died he lived in a hut by the tomb. After mourning he returned to office.

sentences.zh: 吏部尚書褚彥回欲與結婚，秀之不肯，以此頻為兩府外兵參軍。

translations.literal: Director of the Ministry of Personnel Chu Yanhui wished to arrange a marriage with him, but Xiuzhi refused; for this reason he was repeatedly made External Military Aide in the two headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Chu Yanhui, director of the Ministry of Personnel, wanted a marriage alliance, but Xiuzhi refused. For that he was repeatedly posted as external military aide in princely staffs.

sentences.zh: 後為晉平太守，期年求還，或問其故，答曰：「此郡沃壤，珍阜日至，人所昧者財，財生則禍逐，智者不昧財，亦不逐禍。

translations.literal: Later he served as Administrator of Jinping; after one year he requested return, and when someone asked the reason he replied, "This commandery has rich soil; precious goods arrive daily. What men fail to see is that wealth begets calamity in its train. The wise do not fail to see wealth, nor do they pursue calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Later, as administrator of Jinping, he asked to leave after a year. Asked why, he said: "This is rich country. Treasures arrive every day. Men miss the point: wealth draws disaster after it. The wise neither chase wealth nor chase disaster.

sentences.zh: 吾山資已足，豈可久留，以妨賢路。

translations.literal: My mountain resources are already sufficient; how can I long remain and obstruct the path of the worthy?"
translations.idiomatic: I have enough from my hills. How can I stay long and block better men from office?"

sentences.zh: 」乃上表請代。

translations.literal: Thereupon he memorialized requesting a replacement.
translations.idiomatic: He then petitioned for a successor.

sentences.zh: 時人以為王晉平恐富求歸。

translations.literal: People of the time said that Wang of Jinping feared wealth and sought return.
translations.idiomatic: People said Wang of Jinping fled office for fear of growing rich.

sentences.zh: 秀之祖父敬弘性貞正，徐羨之、傅亮當朝，不與來往。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi's grandfather Jinghong's nature was upright and correct; when Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang held the court he did not associate with them.
translations.idiomatic: Xiuzhi's grandfather Jinghong was upright by nature and would not deal with Xu Xianzhi and Fu Liang when they dominated court.

sentences.zh: 及致仕隱吳興，與秀之父瓚之書，深勖以靜退。

translations.literal: When he retired and hid in Wuxing he wrote to Xiuzhi's father Zanzhi, deeply urging quiet withdrawal.
translations.idiomatic: After retiring to Wuxing he wrote to Zanzhi urging him to keep to quiet withdrawal.

sentences.zh: 瓚之為五兵尚書，未嘗詣一朝貴。

translations.literal: Zanzhi served as Director of the Five Armies and never once visited a single court grandee.
translations.idiomatic: Zanzhi, as director of the five armies, never paid a call on any court magnate.

sentences.zh: 江湛謂何偃曰：「王瓚之今便是朝隱。

translations.literal: Jiang Zhan said to He Yan, "Wang Zanzhi today is truly a court recluse."
translations.idiomatic: Jiang Zhan told He Yan: "Wang Zanzhi is a recluse who still holds office."

sentences.zh: 」及柳元景、顏師伯貴要，瓚之竟不侯之。

translations.literal: When Liu Yuanjing and Yan Shibo became powerful and favored, Zanzhi to the end did not wait upon them.
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Yuanjing and Yan Shibo rose to power, Zanzhi never courted them.

sentences.zh: 至秀之為尚書，又不與王儉款接。

translations.literal: When Xiuzhi became Director of the Masters of Writing he also did not cordially associate with Wang Jian.
translations.idiomatic: When Xiuzhi became director of the Masters of Writing, he likewise kept his distance from Wang Jian.

sentences.zh: 三世不事權貴，時人稱之。

translations.literal: For three generations they did not serve the powerful and favored; people of the time praised them.
translations.idiomatic: Three generations refused to serve the mighty. Their contemporaries praised them for it.

sentences.zh: 轉侍中，領射聲校尉。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and concurrently Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot Sound.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary and colonel of the archers who shoot at sound.

sentences.zh: 出為隨王鎮西長史、南郡內史。

translations.literal: He went out as Chief Administrator to the Prince of Sui, General Who Pacifies the West, and Internal Administrator of Nan commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as chief administrator on the staff of the Prince of Sui, general who pacifies the west, and internal administrator of Nan commandery.

sentences.zh: 後為輔國將軍、吳興太守。

translations.literal: Later he served as General Who Assists the State and Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as general who assists the state and administrator of Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 秀之先為諸王長史、行事，便歎曰：「仲祖之識，見於已多。

translations.literal: Xiuzhi had earlier served as chief administrator and acting officer for princes and then sighed, saying, "Zhongzu's discernment has already appeared in me many times."
translations.idiomatic: Having already served as chief administrator and acting officer for princes, Xiuzhi sighed: "Zhongzu's judgment has been proved on me more than once."

sentences.zh: 」便無復仕進，止營理舍亭山宅，有終焉之志。

translations.literal: Thereupon he no longer sought advancement in office, but only managed the Sheting Mountain estate, with the will to end his days there.
translations.idiomatic: He sought no further promotion and only tended his estate at Sheting Mountain, intending to end his days there.

sentences.zh: 及除吳興郡，隱業所在，心願為之。

translations.literal: When he was appointed to Wuxing commandery, the place of his hidden livelihood was where his heart wished to be.
translations.idiomatic: When he was given Wuxing commandery, it was the very country where he had chosen to live apart.

sentences.zh: 到郡修舊山，移置輜重。

translations.literal: On reaching the commandery he restored the old mountain dwelling and moved his baggage there.
translations.idiomatic: On taking up the post he restored his old mountain house and moved his household goods there.

sentences.zh: 隆昌元年卒，遺令「朱服不得入棺，祭則酒脯而已。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longchang he died, leaving instructions: "Scarlet garments must not enter the coffin; in sacrifice let there be only wine and dried meat.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Longchang year 1, leaving orders: "No scarlet robes in the coffin. At the rites, wine and dried meat only.

sentences.zh: 世人以僕妾直靈助哭，當由喪主不能淳至，欲以多聲相亂。

translations.literal: The world uses concubines and servants to assist wailing at the bier; this must be because the chief mourner cannot be pure and thorough, and wishes to use many voices to create confusion.
translations.idiomatic: People hire concubines and servants to wail at the bier because the chief mourner lacks true grief and wants noise to cover the lack.

sentences.zh: 魂而有靈，吾當笑之」。

translations.literal: If the soul has awareness, I shall laugh at this."
translations.idiomatic: If my spirit survives, I will laugh at them."

sentences.zh: 諡曰簡子。

translations.literal: His posthumous title was Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He was posthumously titled Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 延之字希季，升之子也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi, styled Xiji, was the son of Shengzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi, styled Xiji, was Shengzhi's son.

sentences.zh: 少靜默，不交人事。

translations.literal: From youth he was silent and still and did not mix in human affairs.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he was quiet and kept out of worldly affairs.

sentences.zh: 仕宋為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: He served Song as Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he served as left chief administrator of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 清貧，居宇穿漏，褚彥回以啟宋明帝，即敕材官為起三間齋屋。

translations.literal: Poor and upright, his dwelling leaked; Chu Yanhui reported this to Emperor Ming of Song, and the emperor immediately ordered the works office to build three rooms of study hall for him.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in poverty; his roof leaked. Chu Yanhui told Emperor Ming, who at once ordered three study rooms built for him.

sentences.zh: 曆吏部尚書，尚書左僕射。

translations.literal: He successively served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He served in turn as director of the Ministry of Personnel and left vice director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 延之與金紫光祿大夫阮韜俱宋領軍將軍劉湛外甥，並有早譽，湛甚愛之，曰：「韜後當為第一，延之為次也。

translations.literal: Yanzhi and Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel Ruan Tao were both nephews of Song General Who Leads the Army Liu Zhan, and both had early reputation; Zhan greatly loved them and said, "Tao afterward will be first, Yanzhi second."
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi and Grand Master Ruan Tao were both nephews of Liu Zhan, general who leads the army. Both were praised early in life. Zhan favored them and said: "Tao will rank first; Yanzhi second."

sentences.zh: 」延之甚不平。

translations.literal: Yanzhi was very resentful of this.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi resented the remark deeply.

sentences.zh: 每致餉下都，韜與朝士同例，高帝聞之，與延之書曰：「韜雲卿未嘗有別意，當由劉家月旦故邪。

translations.literal: Each time gifts were sent down to the capital, Tao was treated like court gentlemen on the usual model; Emperor Gao heard of this and wrote to Yanzhi, saying, "Has Tao never had a separate intention? Perhaps it is because of the Liu family's monthly ratings?"
translations.idiomatic: Whenever gifts went to the capital, Tao was treated like any other court gentleman. Emperor Gao heard of it and wrote to Yanzhi: "Surely Tao meant no slight. Is this because of the Liu family's monthly rankings?"

sentences.zh: 」韜字長明，陳留人，晉金紫光祿大夫裕玄孫也。

translations.literal: Tao, styled Changming, was a man of Chenliu, great-grandson of Jin Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel Ruan Yu.
translations.idiomatic: Tao, styled Changming, came from Chenliu and was great-grandson of Jin Grand Master Ruan Yu.

sentences.zh: 為南兗州別駕，刺史江夏王義恭逆求資費錢，韜曰：「此朝廷物。

translations.literal: He served as Administrative Aide of South Yanzhou; the Inspector, Prince of Jiangxia Yigong, perversely demanded expense money, and Tao said, "This is the court's property."
translations.idiomatic: As administrative aide of South Yanzhou he faced the prince of Jiangxia, Yigong, who demanded funds improperly. Tao said: "This belongs to the court."

sentences.zh: 」執不與。

translations.literal: He held firm and would not give it.
translations.idiomatic: He refused to hand it over.

sentences.zh: 宋孝武選侍中四人，並以風貌，王彧、謝莊為一雙，韜與何偃為一雙。

translations.literal: Emperor Xiaowu of Song selected four attendants-in-ordinary, all for bearing and appearance: Wang Yu and Xie Zhuang as one pair, Tao and He Yan as one pair.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xiaowu chose four attendants-in-ordinary for their looks: Wang Yu with Xie Zhuang as one pair, Tao with He Yan as another.

sentences.zh: 常充兼假，至始興王師，卒。

translations.literal: He constantly filled concurrent acting posts, up to Tutor to the Prince of Shixing, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He often held acting appointments concurrently, eventually becoming tutor to the Prince of Shixing, and died in office.

sentences.zh: 延之居身簡素，清靜寡欲，凡所經歷，務存不擾。

translations.literal: Yanzhi in personal conduct was simple and plain, pure and still with few desires; in whatever he passed through he strove to keep from disturbing others.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzhi lived simply, desired little, and in every post tried not to disturb others.

sentences.zh: 在江州，祿俸外一無所納。

translations.literal: While in Jiangzhou, beyond salary and stipend he accepted nothing.
translations.idiomatic: At Jiangzhou he took nothing beyond his salary.

sentences.zh: 獨處齋內，未嘗出戶，吏人罕得見焉，雖子弟亦不妄前。

translations.literal: Alone within his study hall he never went outside the door; officials and clerks rarely saw him, and even sons and younger brothers did not rashly approach.
translations.idiomatic: He stayed alone in his study and never crossed the threshold. Clerks seldom saw him; even his sons did not approach casually.

sentences.zh: 時時見親舊，未嘗及世事，從容談詠而已。

translations.literal: From time to time he saw relatives and old friends, but never touched on worldly affairs; only leisurely talk and recitation.
translations.idiomatic: He occasionally received kin and old friends, but never discussed public affairs—only poetry and easy talk.

sentences.zh: 後為尚書左僕射，尋領竟陵王師，卒諡簡子。

translations.literal: Later he served as Left Vice Director of the Masters of Writing; soon he also served as Tutor to the Prince of Jingling, died, posthumous title Jianzi.
translations.idiomatic: He later became left vice director of the Masters of Writing, then tutor to the Prince of Jingling. He died and was posthumously titled Jianzi.

sentences.zh: 子綸之，字元章。

translations.literal: His son was Lunzhi, styled Yuanzhang.
translations.idiomatic: His son Lunzhi was styled Yuanzhang.

sentences.zh: 為安成王記室參軍，偃仰召會，退居僚末。

translations.literal: He served as Recording Secretary to the Prince of Ancheng; at summons and assembly he reclined at ease, withdrawing to the rear among the staff.
translations.idiomatic: As recording secretary to the Prince of Ancheng, he lounged at ease when called to meetings and kept to the rear of the staff.

sentences.zh: 司徒袁粲聞而歎曰：「格外之官，便今日為重。

translations.literal: Minister of Education Yuan Can heard this and sighed, saying, "An extraordinary office has from today become weighty."
translations.idiomatic: Minister of Education Yuan Can sighed when he heard of it: "A post outside the usual ladder has become prestigious overnight."

sentences.zh: 」貴游居此位者，遂以不掌文記為高，自綸之始也。

translations.literal: Noble travelers who held this post thereupon took not handling written records as lofty; this began with Lunzhi.
translations.idiomatic: After Lunzhi, noblemen in that post began to treat refusal to keep written records as a mark of distinction.

sentences.zh: 齊永明中，歷位侍中，出為豫章太守。

translations.literal: In the Yongming era of Qi he successively served as Attendant-in-Ordinary and went out as Administrator of Yuzhang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi in the Yongming era he rose to attendant-in-ordinary and then left court as administrator of Yuzhang.

sentences.zh: 下車祭徐孺子、許子將墓，圖畫陳蕃、華歆、謝鯤像於郡朝堂。

translations.literal: On taking office he sacrificed at the tombs of Xu Ruzi and Xu Zijiang, and painted portraits of Chen Fan, Hua Xin, and Xie Kun in the commandery audience hall.
translations.idiomatic: On taking office he offered sacrifice at the tombs of Xu Ruzi and Xu Zijiang and hung portraits of Chen Fan, Hua Xin, and Xie Kun in the commandery hall.

sentences.zh: 為政寬簡，稱良二千石。

translations.literal: His governance was broad and simple; he was called a good administrator of two thousand shi.
translations.idiomatic: His rule was lenient and plain, and men called him an excellent commandery administrator.

sentences.zh: 武帝幸琅邪城，綸之與光祿大夫全景文等二十一人坐不參承，為有司奏免官。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu visited Langya city, Lunzhi together with Grand Master of the Bright Hall Quan Jingwen and twenty-one others sat without attending the reception and were reported by the responsible office and removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu visited Langya, Lunzhi and Grand Master Quan Jingwen plus twenty-one others failed to attend the reception. The responsible office reported them and they were dismissed.

sentences.zh: 後位侍中、都官尚書，卒。

translations.literal: Later he held the posts of Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Punishments, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as attendant-in-ordinary and director of the Ministry of Punishments, then died.

sentences.zh: 自敬弘至綸之，並方嚴，皆克日乃見子孫，蓋家風也。

translations.literal: From Jinghong to Lunzhi they were all stern and square, all meeting sons and grandsons only on fixed days—this was the family style.
translations.idiomatic: From Jinghong to Lunzhi the family was uniformly austere: descendants were received only on appointed days. That was their household way.

sentences.zh: 綸之子昕，有業行，居父憂過禮。

translations.literal: Lunzhi's son Xin had solid conduct; in mourning for his father he exceeded the rites.
translations.idiomatic: Lunzhi's son Xin was a man of solid character and mourned his father beyond what the rites required.

sentences.zh: 謝伷欲遣參之，孔珪曰：「何假參，此豈有全理。

translations.literal: Xie Zhou wished to send someone to attend him; Kong Gui said, "Why send an attendant? This surely has no whole principle."
translations.idiomatic: Xie Zhou wanted to send an attendant to him. Kong Gui said: "Why send anyone? There is no saving this."

sentences.zh: 」以憂卒。

translations.literal: He died of grief.
translations.idiomatic: He died of grief.

sentences.zh: 峻字茂遠，秀之子也。

translations.literal: Jun, styled Maoyuan, was the son of Xiuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Jun, styled Maoyuan, was Xiuzhi's son.

sentences.zh: 少美風姿，善容止。

translations.literal: From youth he had fine bearing and mien and was skilled in deportment.
translations.idiomatic: From youth he had fine looks and graceful bearing.

sentences.zh: 仕齊為桂陽內史。

translations.literal: He served Qi as Internal Administrator of Guiyang.
translations.idiomatic: Under Qi he served as internal administrator of Guiyang.

sentences.zh: 梁天監初，為中書侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Tianjian under Liang he served as Vice Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of the Tianjian era under Liang he became vice director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 武帝甚悅其風采，與陳郡謝覽同見賞擢。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu greatly delighted in his bearing and mien; together with Xie Lan of Chen commandery he was seen and promoted.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu admired his bearing and promoted him together with Xie Lan of Chen commandery.

sentences.zh: 累遷侍中，吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant-in-Ordinary and Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to attendant-in-ordinary and director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 處選甚得名譽。

translations.literal: In handling selection he greatly gained reputation for name.
translations.idiomatic: In appointments he won a strong reputation.

sentences.zh: 峻性詳雅，無趨競心，嘗與謝覽約，官至侍中，不復謀進仕。

translations.literal: Jun's nature was detailed and refined, without a mind to rush and compete; once he agreed with Xie Lan that when they reached Attendant-in-Ordinary they would no longer seek further advancement.
translations.idiomatic: Jun was meticulous and unambitious. He and Xie Lan agreed that once they reached attendant-in-ordinary they would seek no further promotion.

sentences.zh: 覽自吏部尚書出為吳興郡，平心不畏強禦，亦由處俗情薄故也。

translations.literal: Lan from Director of the Ministry of Personnel went out as Administrator of Wuxing commandery; with a level heart he did not fear the strong and overbearing, also because the customs of the age were thin.
translations.idiomatic: Lan left the Ministry of Personnel to govern Wuxing. Impartial and fearless, he could act so because the age had grown coarse.

sentences.zh: 峻為侍中已後，雖不退身，亦淡然自守，無所營務。

translations.literal: After Jun became Attendant-in-Ordinary, although he did not withdraw from office, he also calmly kept himself and had no affairs to manage.
translations.idiomatic: After becoming attendant-in-ordinary Jun did not resign, but he kept to himself and undertook no new business.

sentences.zh: 遷金紫光祿大夫，未拜，卒，諡惠子。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel, did not accept appointment, died, posthumous title Huizi.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to grand master of the bright hall with golden tassel, declined the appointment, and died. He was posthumously titled Huizi.

sentences.zh: 子琮為國子生，尚始興王女繁昌主。

translations.literal: Jun's son Cong was a student at the Imperial University and married the Princess Fanchang, daughter of the Prince of Shixing.
translations.idiomatic: Jun's son Cong studied at the imperial university and married Princess Fanchang, daughter of the Prince of Shixing.

sentences.zh: 琮不慧，為學生所嗤，遂離婚。

translations.literal: Cong was not clever and was mocked by fellow students; thereupon the marriage was dissolved.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was dull-witted and ridiculed by his classmates, and the marriage was annulled.

sentences.zh: 峻謝王，王曰：「此自上意，僕極不願如此。

translations.literal: Jun apologized to the prince; the prince said, "This came from above; I myself extremely did not wish it so."
translations.idiomatic: Jun apologized to the prince, who said: "This was the emperor's will. I never wanted it."

sentences.zh: 」峻曰：「下官曾祖是謝仁祖外孫，亦不藉殿下姻媾為門戶耳。」

translations.literal: Jun said, "Your humble servant's great-grandfather was the maternal grandson of Xie Renzu; I also do not rely on marriage alliance with Your Highness for my family's standing."
translations.idiomatic: Jun replied: "My great-grandfather was Xie Renzu's grandson by a daughter. Our house does not need Your Highness's marriage to stand."

sentences.zh: 王鎮之字伯重，晉司州刺史胡之之從孫、而裕之從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhenzhi, styled Bozhong, was the grandnephew of Jin Inspector of Sizhou Hu Zhi and the younger cousin once removed of Yuzhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhenzhi, styled Bozhong, was grandnephew of Jin inspector of Sizhou Hu Zhi and a cousin once removed of Yuzhi.

sentences.zh: 祖耆之，位中書郎，父隨之，上虞令。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Qizhi, who held the post of Director of the Secretariat; his father Suizhi was Magistrate of Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Qizhi had been director of the secretariat; his father Suizhi was magistrate of Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 鎮之為剡、上虞令，並有能名。

translations.literal: Zhenzhi served as Magistrate of Shan and Shangyu, both with reputation for ability.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenzhi served as magistrate of Shan and of Shangyu, earning a name for competence in both posts.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，以為大將軍錄事參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin he was made Recording Aide to the Grand General.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan controlled Jin, Zhenzhi was made recording aide to the grand general.

sentences.zh: 時三吳饑荒，遣鎮之銜命賑恤，而會稽內史王愉不奉符旨，鎮之依事糾奏。

translations.literal: At that time the Three Wu region suffered famine; he was sent with imperial commission to relieve and succor, but the Internal Administrator of Kuaiji Wang Yu did not follow the written order; Zhenzhi according to the matter impeached and memorialized.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Wu lands were starving he was sent to distribute relief, but Kuaiji's internal administrator Wang Yu ignored the order. Zhenzhi impeached him according to law.

sentences.zh: 愉子綏，玄之外甥，當時貴盛，鎮之為所排抑。

translations.literal: Yu's son Sui was Xuan's nephew by marriage; at the time he was noble and flourishing, and Zhenzhi was pushed aside and suppressed by him.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yu's son Sui was Huan Xuan's nephew by marriage and then at the height of power. Zhenzhi was sidelined and suppressed.

sentences.zh: 以母老求補安成太守，以母憂去職。

translations.literal: Because his mother was old he requested supplementary appointment as Administrator of Ancheng and left office on account of mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: His mother being old, he asked to be made administrator of Ancheng and left office when she died.

sentences.zh: 在官清潔，妻子無以自反，乃棄家致喪還上虞舊墓。

translations.literal: In office he was pure and clean; wife and children had no means to return home, and therefore he abandoned the household and conducted the mourning back to the old tomb at Shangyu.
translations.idiomatic: He served with integrity, but his family had no money to travel. He gave up his household and brought the funeral home to the old grave at Shangyu.

sentences.zh: 葬畢，為子標之求安復令，隨子之官。

translations.literal: When burial was finished he sought for his son Biaozhi the post of Magistrate of Anfu and followed his son to office.
translations.idiomatic: After the burial he secured for his son Biaozhi the magistracy of Anfu and went with him to his post.

sentences.zh: 服闋，為征西道規司馬、南平太守。

translations.literal: When mourning ended he served as Military Administrator to General Who Conquers the West Daogui and Administrator of Nanping.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended he became military administrator on Daogui's staff and administrator of Nanping.

sentences.zh: 後為御史中丞，執正不撓，百僚憚之。

translations.literal: Later he served as Imperial Censor and was upright and unbending; the hundred officials feared him.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as imperial censor, upright and unyielding. The whole bureaucracy feared him.

sentences.zh: 出為建威將軍、平越中郎將、廣州刺史，加都督。

translations.literal: He went out as General Who Establishes Might, General of the Army Who Pacifies the Yue, Inspector of Guangzhou, with additional command authority.
translations.idiomatic: He left court as general who establishes might, general of the army who pacifies the Yue, and inspector of Guangzhou, with overall command.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝謂人曰：「鎮之少著清績，必將繼美吳隱，嶺南弊俗，非此不康也。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu of Song said to others, "Zhenzhi from youth has shown pure achievements; he will surely continue the excellence of Wu Yinshi. The corrupt customs of Lingnan will not be set right without this man."
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu said: "Zhenzhi has been upright from youth. He will follow Wu Yinshi's example. Lingnan's corrupt ways will not be cured without him."

sentences.zh: 」在鎮不受俸祿，蕭然無營，去官之日，不異初至。

translations.literal: While in the post he did not accept salary and stipend; he was austere without enterprise; on the day he left office it was no different from when he first arrived.
translations.idiomatic: In office he took no salary beyond what was due and lived sparely. When he left, he had nothing more than when he arrived.

sentences.zh: 武帝初建相國府，為諮議參軍，領錄事。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu first established the office of the Chancellor of State he served as Advisory Aide and concurrently Chief of Records.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu first formed the chancellor's office, Zhenzhi served as advisory aide and chief of records.

sentences.zh: 善於吏職，嚴而不殘。

translations.literal: He was skilled in clerical duties, strict yet not cruel.
translations.idiomatic: He was skilled in administration—strict but not harsh.

sentences.zh: 遷宋台祠部尚書。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Rites of the Song Platform.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to director of the Ministry of Rites on the Song platform.

sentences.zh: 武帝踐阼，卒于宣訓衛尉。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne he died at Xuanxun Commandant of the Guard.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Zhenzhi died while serving as commandant of Xuanxun guard.

sentences.zh: 弟弘之。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Hongzhi.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Hongzhi.

sentences.zh: 弘之字方平，少孤貧，為外祖征士何准所撫育，從叔獻之及太原王恭並貴重之。

translations.literal: Hongzhi, styled Fangping, from youth was orphaned and poor; he was reared by his maternal grandfather, the reclusive scholar He Zhun, and his father's younger cousin Xianzhi together with Wang Gong of Taiyuan all valued and honored him.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi, styled Fangping, was orphaned young and poor. His maternal grandfather, the recluse He Zhun, raised him. His cousin Xianzhi and Wang Gong of Taiyuan both held him in esteem.

sentences.zh: 仕晉為司徒主簿。

translations.literal: He served Jin as Chief Clerk of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Under Jin he served as chief clerk to the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 家貧，性好山水，求為烏傷令。

translations.literal: The family was poor; his nature loved mountains and waters, and he requested appointment as Magistrate of Wushang.
translations.idiomatic: The family was poor and he loved mountains and rivers, so he asked to be magistrate of Wushang.

sentences.zh: 桓玄輔晉，桓謙以為衛軍參軍。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan assisted Jin, Huan Qian made him Military Aide in the Guard Army.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan controlled Jin, Huan Qian made him military aide in the guard army.

sentences.zh: 時殷仲文還姑孰，祖送傾朝，謙要弘之同行，答曰：「凡祖離送別，必在有情，下官與殷風馬不接，無緣扈從。

translations.literal: At that time Yin Zhongwen returned to Gudu; the court saw him off in full assembly; Qian wanted Hongzhi to go together, and he replied, "Whenever one sees off at parting, it must be among those with feeling; your humble servant and Yin have no wind-horse connection and no reason to follow in attendance."
translations.idiomatic: When Yin Zhongwen returned to Gudu the whole court turned out to see him off. Qian wanted Hongzhi to join the procession. Hongzhi answered: "One sees off only those one cares for. Yin and I share no bond. I have no cause to follow."

sentences.zh: 」謙貴其言。

translations.literal: Qian valued his words.
translations.idiomatic: Qian respected his reply.

sentences.zh: 母隨兄鎮之之安成郡，弘之解職同行。

translations.literal: His mother followed his elder brother Zhenzhi to Ancheng commandery; Hongzhi resigned office and went together.
translations.idiomatic: When his mother went with his brother Zhenzhi to Ancheng, Hongzhi resigned and went with them.

sentences.zh: 義熙中，何無忌及宋武帝辟召，一無所就。

translations.literal: In the Yixi era He Wuji and Emperor Wu of Song summoned and called him; he accepted none.
translations.idiomatic: During Yixi, He Wuji and Emperor Wu both summoned him. He answered none of their calls.

sentences.zh: 弘之元嘉四年卒，顏延之欲為作誄，書與其子曇生曰：「君家高世之善，有識歸重，豫染豪翰，所應載述，況僕托慕末風，竊以敘德為事，但恨短筆不足書美。

translations.literal: Hongzhi died in the fourth year of Yuanjia; Yan Yanzhi wished to compose a eulogy for him and wrote to his son Tansheng, saying, "Your family's excellence spanning generations, men of discernment turn to it in respect; to brush the noble writing one ought to record it—how much more when I, trusting to admiration of the late wind, privately take narrating virtue as my affair, yet regret my short brush is insufficient to write the beauty."
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi died in Yuanjia year 4. Yan Yanzhi wanted to write his eulogy and wrote to his son Tansheng: "Your family's virtue across generations commands respect. I hoped to set it down, trusting my admiration for your house, but my pen is too short for the task."

sentences.zh: 」誄竟不就。

translations.literal: The eulogy in the end was not completed.
translations.idiomatic: The eulogy was never written.

sentences.zh: 曇生好文義，以謙和見稱，曆吏部尚書，太常卿。

translations.literal: Tansheng loved literary principles and was praised for modesty and harmony; he successively served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Tansheng loved letters and was known for modesty. He served as director of the Ministry of Personnel and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 孝武末，為吳興太守。

translations.literal: At the end of Xiaowu he served as Administrator of Wuxing.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Emperor Xiaowu's reign he governed Wuxing.

sentences.zh: 明帝初興，與四方同逆，戰敗歸降，被宥，終於中散大夫。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Mingdi's rise he joined the four directions in rebellion; defeated in battle he returned and surrendered, was pardoned, and ended as Grand Master of Palace Leisure.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming rose, Tansheng joined the rebels, was defeated, surrendered, was pardoned, and ended as grand master of palace leisure.

sentences.zh: 阮萬齡，陳留尉氏人。

translations.literal: Ruan Wanling was a man of Weishi in Chenliu.
translations.idiomatic: Ruan Wanling came from Weishi in Chenliu.

sentences.zh: 祖思曠，左光祿大夫。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Sikuo, Left Grand Master of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Sikuo was left grand master of the bright hall.

sentences.zh: 父甯，黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: His father was Ning, Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ning was attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 萬齡少知名，為孟昶建威長史。

translations.literal: Wanling from youth had known name and served as Chief Administrator to Meng Chang, General Who Establishes Might.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling was known from youth and served as chief administrator to Meng Chang, general who establishes might.

sentences.zh: 時袁豹、江夷相系為昶司馬，時人謂昶府有三素望。

translations.literal: At the time Yuan Bao and Jiang Yi in succession served as Chang's Military Administrator; people of the time said Chang's headquarters had three men of pure reputation.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Bao and Jiang Yi served in turn as Chang's military administrator. People said Chang's staff had three men of unblemished repute.

sentences.zh: 萬齡家在會稽剡縣，頗有素情，位左戶尚書，太常。

translations.literal: Wanling's family was in Shan county of Kuaiji; he had quite pure feeling and held the posts of Director of the Left Households and Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: Wanling's family was in Shan county, Kuaiji. He lived with plain tastes and served as director of the left households and minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 出為湘州刺史，無政績。

translations.literal: He went out as Inspector of Xiangzhou and had no administrative achievements.
translations.idiomatic: As inspector of Xiangzhou he left no mark in office.

sentences.zh: 後為散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫，卒。

translations.literal: Later he served as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as supernumerary regular attendant and grand master of the bright hall with golden tassel, then died.

sentences.zh: 曇生弟普曜，位秘書監。

translations.literal: Tansheng's younger brother Puyao held the post of Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Tansheng's brother Puyao became director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 普曜子晏。

translations.literal: Puyao's son was Yan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan was Puyao's son.

sentences.zh: 晏字休默，一字士彥。

translations.literal: Yan, styled Xiumo, also styled Shiyan.
translations.idiomatic: Yan, styled Xiumo, also known as Shiyan.

sentences.zh: 仕宋，初為建安國左常侍，稍至車騎，晉熙王燮安西板晏主簿，時齊武帝為長史，與晏相遇。

translations.literal: He served Song; at first he was Left Attendant-in-Ordinary of the Principality of Jian'an, gradually reaching Chariots and Cavalry; Prince of Jinxi Xie appointed Yan chief clerk on his western headquarters board, and at the time Emperor Wu of Qi was chief administrator; he and Yan met.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he began as left attendant of the Principality of Jian'an and rose to the chariots-and-cavalry office. Prince Xie of Jinxi made Yan chief clerk on his western staff while the future Emperor Wu of Qi was chief administrator. The two men met there.

sentences.zh: 府轉鎮西，板晏為記室。

translations.literal: When the headquarters shifted to Pacify-the-West, Yan was appointed on the board as Recording Secretary.
translations.idiomatic: When the staff became the Pacify-the-West headquarters, Yan was made recording secretary.

sentences.zh: 沈攸之事難，隨武帝鎮盆城。

translations.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair became difficult he followed Emperor Wu in garrisoning Pencheng.
translations.idiomatic: During Shen Youzhi's rebellion he followed the future emperor to garrison Pencheng.

sentences.zh: 齊高帝時威權雖重，而眾情猶有疑惑，晏便專心奉事，軍旅書翰皆見委。

translations.literal: At the time of Emperor Gao of Qi, although authority and power were heavy, popular sentiment still had doubts; Yan then devoted his heart to serving him, and military and camp letters and documents were all entrusted to him.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gao of Qi held power, doubt still lingered among men. Yan devoted himself to the cause, and military correspondence was entrusted to him.

sentences.zh: 性甚便僻，漸見親待，常參議機密。

translations.literal: His nature was very accommodating and clever; he was gradually seen and treated with intimacy, and constantly participated in deliberating secret matters.
translations.idiomatic: Facile and quick-witted, he grew intimate with the emperor and was often drawn into secret deliberations.

sentences.zh: 建元初，為太子中庶子。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he served as Junior Mentor in the Eastern Palace.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyuan he became junior mentor in the eastern palace.

sentences.zh: 武帝在東宮，專斷朝事，多不聞啟，晏慮及罪，稱疾自疏。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu was in the Eastern Palace he alone decided court affairs; many matters were not reported upward; Yan feared reaching guilt and claimed illness to distance himself.
translations.idiomatic: While the future Emperor Wu ran the eastern palace he decided much of court business without reporting upward. Yan, fearing blame, feigned illness and kept his distance.

sentences.zh: 武帝即位，為長兼侍中，意任如舊。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne he served as Attendant-in-Ordinary concurrently and long, with trust and commission as before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu took the throne Yan served as long-attendant-in-ordinary with the same trust as before.

sentences.zh: 遷侍中祭酒。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary Libationer.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to attendant-in-ordinary libationer.

sentences.zh: 遭母喪，起為司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Encountering mourning for his mother, he was recalled to serve as Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Called back from mourning for his mother, he served as left chief administrator of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 晏父普曜藉晏勢，多曆通官。

translations.literal: Yan's father Puyao relied on Yan's power and repeatedly held posts passing through offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's father Puyao used his son's influence to hold one passing appointment after another.

sentences.zh: 普曜卒，晏居喪有禮。

translations.literal: When Puyao died Yan observed mourning with propriety.
translations.idiomatic: When Puyao died Yan mourned with proper rites.

sentences.zh: 永明六年，為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Yongming he served as Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 6 he became intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 晏位任親重，自豫章王嶷、尚書令王儉皆降意接之，而晏每以疏漏被責，連稱疾。

translations.literal: Yan's position and commission were intimate and weighty; from Prince of Yuzhang Xiao and Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian all lowered intent to receive him, yet Yan repeatedly because of oversights was reproved and repeatedly claimed illness.
translations.idiomatic: Yan held intimate and heavy power. Even Prince Xiao of Yuzhang and Director Wang Jian deferred to him, yet he was often rebuked for lapses and repeatedly pleaded illness.

sentences.zh: 久之，轉為江州刺史，泣不願出，留為吏部尚書、太子右率，終以舊恩見寵。

translations.literal: After long time he was transferred to Inspector of Jiangzhou; weeping he did not wish to go out, was retained as Director of the Ministry of Personnel and Right Leader of the Heir Apparent, and to the end because of old favor was shown favor.
translations.idiomatic: Eventually he was sent to Jiangzhou as inspector. He wept and refused to leave, was kept as director of the Ministry of Personnel and right leader of the heir apparent, and to the end enjoyed favor for old service.

sentences.zh: 時尚書令王儉雖貴而疏，晏既領選，權行台閣，與儉頗不平。

translations.literal: At the time Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian, although noble, was distant; Yan since he also handled selection exercised power in the secretariat tower and was quite at odds with Jian.
translations.idiomatic: Director Wang Jian was grand but distant. Yan, who also controlled appointments, wielded secretariat power and clashed with him.

sentences.zh: 儉卒，禮官欲依王導諡為「文獻」，晏啟上曰：「導乃得此諡，但宋來不加素族。

translations.literal: When Jian died the Masters of Rites wished to follow Wang Dao in enfeoffing the posthumous title "Literary and Presented," and Yan memorialized the emperor, saying, "Dao obtained this posthumous title, but since Song none has been added for plain clans."
translations.idiomatic: When Jian died the rites officers wanted to follow Wang Dao's example and posthumously title him "Literary and Presented." Yan memorialized: "Dao earned that title, but since Song plain families have not received it."

sentences.zh: 」謂親人曰：「平頭憲事已行矣。

translations.literal: He said to kinsmen, "Pingtou Xian's affair has already been carried out."
translations.idiomatic: He told his kin: "The business with Pingtou Xian is done."

sentences.zh: 」十一年，為右僕射，領太孫右衛率。

translations.literal: In the eleventh year he served as Right Vice Director and concurrently Right Leader of Guard for the Grand Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: In year 11 he became right vice director and right leader of guard for the grand heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 武帝崩，遺旨以尚書事付晏及徐孝嗣。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu died his final instruction entrusted affairs of the Masters of Writing to Yan and Xu Xiaosi.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu's deathbed order entrusted the Masters of Writing to Yan and Xu Xiaosi.

sentences.zh: 郁林即位，轉左僕射。

translations.literal: When Prince of Yulin ascended he was transferred to Left Vice Director.
translations.idiomatic: When Prince of Yulin ascended, Yan became left vice director.

sentences.zh: 及明帝謀廢立，晏便回應推奉，轉尚書令，封曲江縣侯，給鼓吹一部，甲仗五十人入殿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Ming plotted deposition and installation Yan at once responded in support and promotion; he was transferred to Director of the Masters of Writing, enfeoffed as Marquis of Qujiang county, granted one set of drum-and-pipe music, fifty armored guards entering the hall.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Ming plotted to depose and install emperors, Yan at once backed him. He became director of the Masters of Writing, was enfeoffed as marquis of Qujiang, and given drums, pipes, and fifty armored guards in the hall.

sentences.zh: 時明帝形勢已布，而莫敢先言，蕭諶兄弟握兵權，遲疑未決，晏頻三夜微步詣諶議，時人以此窺之。

translations.literal: At the time Emperor Ming's situation was already arranged, yet none dared speak first; the Xiao Chen brothers held military power and hesitated without decision; Yan for three nights in succession walked secretly to Chen's place to deliberate; people of the time used this to peer into him.
translations.idiomatic: Ming's coup was ready, but no one spoke first. The Xiao Chen brothers held the army and hesitated. Yan stole out three nights running to consult Chen. Men read his movements as proof of complicity.

sentences.zh: 明帝與晏東府語及時事，晏抵掌曰：「公常言晏怯，今定如何？

translations.literal: Emperor Ming with Yan in the Eastern Palace spoke of current affairs; Yan struck his palm and said, "Your Grace always says Yan is timid—how is it fixed now?"
translations.idiomatic: Ming discussed affairs with Yan in the eastern palace. Yan slapped his palm: "You always call me timid. What do you think now?"

sentences.zh: 」建武元年，進號驃騎大將軍，給班劍二十人，又加兵百人，領太子少傅，進爵為公。

translations.literal: In the first year of Jianwu he was advanced in title to General of Agile Cavalry, granted twenty guards with ceremonial swords, also added one hundred soldiers, served as Junior Tutor to the Heir Apparent, and advanced in rank to duke.
translations.idiomatic: In Jianwu year 1 he was promoted to general of agile cavalry with twenty guards bearing ceremonial swords, given another hundred troops, made junior tutor to the heir apparent, and raised to duke.

sentences.zh: 以魏軍動，給兵千人。

translations.literal: Because Wei armies were active, one thousand soldiers were granted.
translations.idiomatic: When Wei armies moved, he was granted a thousand troops.

sentences.zh: 晏人望未重，又與上素疏，中興初，雖以事計委任，而內相疑阻，晏無防意。

translations.literal: Yan's popular esteem was not yet heavy, and moreover he had from the first been distant from the emperor; at the beginning of Restoration, although affairs were entrusted to him by plan, inwardly there was mutual suspicion and obstruction; Yan had no mind of guard.
translations.idiomatic: Yan lacked broad prestige and had always been distant from the emperor. Early in Restoration he was entrusted with business, yet mutual suspicion remained. Yan kept no guard.

sentences.zh: 既居朝端，事多專決，內外要職，並用周旋門義，每與上爭用人。

translations.literal: Once he occupied the head of court, affairs were mostly decided by him alone; inside and outside important posts all used his rotating gate clients; each time he contended with the emperor over appointing men.
translations.idiomatic: At the head of court he decided most matters himself, filled key posts with his clients, and repeatedly fought the emperor over appointments.

sentences.zh: 數呼相工自視，雲當大貴。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he summoned physiognomists to look at himself; they said he ought to reach great nobility.
translations.idiomatic: He often called in physiognomists who told him he was destined for the highest rank.

sentences.zh: 與客語，好屏人。

translations.literal: When speaking with guests he liked to send people away from the screen.
translations.idiomatic: When he talked with guests he liked to dismiss attendants from the room.

sentences.zh: 上聞，疑晏欲反，遂有誅晏意。

translations.literal: The emperor heard of this, suspected Yan wished to rebel, and thereupon had the intention to execute Yan.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor heard of it, suspected Yan of plotting rebellion, and resolved to kill him.

sentences.zh: 有鮮于文粲與晏子德元往來，密探朝旨，告晏有異志。

translations.literal: There was Xianyu Wencan who went back and forth with Yan's son Deyuan, secretly probing court intent and reporting to Yan that he had a different will.
translations.idiomatic: Xianyu Wencan consorted with Yan's son Deyuan, spied on court opinion, and told Yan he was suspected of disloyalty.

sentences.zh: 又左右單景雋、陳世范等采巫覡言啟上，雲晏懷異圖。

translations.literal: Also attendants Shan Jingjun and Chen Shifan and others gathered words of shamans and sorcerers to report to the emperor, saying Yan harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Attendants Shan Jingjun and Chen Shifan also collected sorcerers' talk and told the emperor Yan harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 是時南郊應親奉，景雋等言晏因此與武帝故主帥于道中竊發。

translations.literal: At that time the southern suburban sacrifice ought to have been personally attended; Jingjun and others said Yan would therefore with the late Emperor Wu's former chief commander launch a secret attack on the road.
translations.idiomatic: The southern sacrifice required the emperor's presence. Jingjun claimed Yan would use the occasion to strike along the road with the late emperor's former commander.

sentences.zh: 會獸犯郊壇，帝愈懼，未郊前一日，上乃停行，先報晏及徐孝嗣，孝嗣奉旨，而晏陳郊祀事大，必宜自力。

translations.literal: It happened that beasts violated the suburban altar; the emperor grew more fearful; one day before the sacrifice the emperor stopped the journey, first reporting to Yan and Xu Xiaosi; Xiaosi received the instruction, but Yan declared the suburban sacrifice a great affair and that one must surely exert oneself.
translations.idiomatic: Beasts desecrated the suburban altar and the emperor grew afraid. A day before the rites he halted the procession and warned Yan and Xu Xiaosi. Xiaosi obeyed, but Yan insisted the sacrifice must be conducted in person.

sentences.zh: 景雋言益見信，元會畢，乃召晏于華林省誅之。

translations.literal: Jingjun's words were increasingly believed; when the New Year audience ended the emperor then summoned Yan to Hualin Pavilion and executed him.
translations.idiomatic: Jingjun's story gained credence. After the New Year audience the emperor summoned Yan to Hualin Pavilion and had him killed.

sentences.zh: 下詔顯其罪，稱以河東王鉉識用微弱，欲令守以虛器，並令收付廷尉。

translations.literal: An edict displayed his crimes, saying that because Prince of Hedong Xuan's discernment and use were slight, he wished to make him guard an empty vessel, and ordered all seized and delivered to the Court of Judicial Review.
translations.idiomatic: An edict listed his crimes, claiming Prince Xuan of Hedong was too weak to rule and had been kept as a figurehead, and ordered his associates sent to the Court of Judicial Review.

sentences.zh: 晏之為員外郎也，父普曜齋前柏樹忽變成梧桐，論者以為梧桐雖有棲鳳之美，而失後凋之節。

translations.literal: When Yan was an supernumerary gentleman his father Puyao's cypress before the fasting hall suddenly changed into a parasol tree; discussers said the parasol tree although has the beauty of nesting phoenixes yet loses the virtue of lasting through winter.
translations.idiomatic: While Yan was an supernumerary gentleman, a cypress before Puyao's fasting hall turned into a parasol tree. Men said the parasol may invite the phoenix but lacks the cypress's virtue of surviving winter.

sentences.zh: 及晏敗，果如之。

translations.literal: When Yan was defeated it indeed was so.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan fell, the omen proved true.

sentences.zh: 又未敗前，見屋桷子悉是大蛇，就視之猶木也。

translations.literal: Also before defeat he saw the rafter ends of the house all as great serpents; going close to look they were still wood.
translations.idiomatic: Before his fall he saw every rafter-end as a great serpent; up close they were still wood.

sentences.zh: 晏惡之，乃以紙裹桷子，猶紙內搖動，蔌蔌有聲。

translations.literal: Yan hated this and therefore wrapped the rafter ends in paper; still within the paper they shook with a rustling sound.
translations.idiomatic: He hated the sight and wrapped the rafters in paper, yet the paper still rustled as if something moved inside.

sentences.zh: 又於北山廟答賽夜還，晏醉，部伍人亦飲酒，羽儀錯亂，前後十餘里中，不復禁制。

translations.literal: Also on returning from answering sacrifice at the northern mountain shrine at night, Yan was drunk; the escort men also drank wine; insignia fell into disorder, and for more than ten li before and after no restraint was enforced.
translations.idiomatic: Returning drunk at night from sacrifice at the northern mountain shrine, he and his escort drank until the procession fell into disorder for more than ten li.

sentences.zh: 識者雲此不復久也。

translations.literal: Men of discernment said this would not long continue.
translations.idiomatic: Those who read omens said he could not last long.

sentences.zh: 未幾而敗。

translations.literal: Before long he was defeated.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 晏子德元，有意尚，位車騎長史。

translations.literal: Yan's son Deyuan had intent and aspiration and held the post of Chief Administrator of Chariots and Cavalry.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's son Deyuan was a man of purpose and served as chief administrator of the chariots-and-cavalry office.

sentences.zh: 德元初名湛，武帝曰：「劉湛、江湛，並不善終，此非佳名也。

translations.literal: Deyuan's original name was Zhan; Emperor Wu said, "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both did not end well; this is not a fine name."
translations.idiomatic: Deyuan had originally been named Zhan. Emperor Wu said: "Liu Zhan and Jiang Zhan both came to bad ends. This is no auspicious name."

sentences.zh: 」晏乃改之，至是及誅。

translations.literal: Yan thereupon changed it; at this time he reached execution together with him.
translations.idiomatic: Yan changed the name, but when the purge came Deyuan was killed with him.

sentences.zh: 晏弟詡，位少府卿。

translations.literal: Yan's younger brother Xu held the post of Minister of the Lesser Treasury.
translations.idiomatic: Yan's younger brother Xu served as minister of the lesser treasury.

sentences.zh: 敕未登黃門郎，不得畜女伎，詡與射聲校尉陰玄智坐畜伎免官，禁錮十年。

translations.literal: An edict had it that one who had not reached Attendant at the Yellow Gate must not keep female performers; Xu together with Colonel of the Archers Who Shoot Sound Yin Xuanzhi sat because of keeping performers, was removed from office, and confined for ten years.
translations.idiomatic: An edict forbade men below attendant at the yellow gate to keep female performers. Xu and Colonel Yin Xuanzhi were dismissed and confined for ten years for keeping performers.

sentences.zh: 敕特原詡。

translations.literal: An edict specially pardoned Xu.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor issued a special pardon for Xu.

sentences.zh: 詡亦篤舊。

translations.literal: Xu also was devoted to old friendships.
translations.idiomatic: Xu was also loyal to old friends.

sentences.zh: 後拜廣州刺史。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Inspector of Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: He was later appointed inspector of Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 晏誅，上遣殺之。

translations.literal: When Yan was executed the emperor sent men to kill him.
translations.idiomatic: When Yan was executed the emperor sent men to kill Xu as well.

sentences.zh: 思遠、晏從父弟也。

translations.literal: Siyuan was Yan's younger cousin.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan and Yan were cousins; Siyuan was the younger.

sentences.zh: 父羅雲，平西長史。

translations.literal: His father was Luoyun, Chief Administrator Who Pacifies the West.
translations.idiomatic: His father Luoyun had been chief administrator on the Pacify-the-West staff.

sentences.zh: 思遠八歲父卒，祖弘之及外祖新安太守羊敬元並棲退高尚，故思遠少無仕心。

translations.literal: When Siyuan was eight his father died; his grandfather Hongzhi and maternal grandfather, Administrator of Xin'an Yang Jingyuan, both dwelt in retirement with lofty character; therefore Siyuan from youth had no mind to take office.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan was eight when his father died. His grandfather Hongzhi and maternal grandfather Yang Jingyuan, administrator of Xin'an, both lived in lofty retirement, so from youth Siyuan had no wish for office.

sentences.zh: 宋建平王景素辟南徐州主簿，深見禮遇。

translations.literal: Prince of Jianping Jing Su recruited him as Chief Clerk of South Xuzhou and deeply showed him ritual courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Jing Su of Jianping recruited him as chief clerk of South Xuzhou and treated him with great honor.

sentences.zh: 景素被誅，左右離散，思遠親視殯葬，手種松柏，與廬江何昌宇、沛郡劉璡上表理之，事感朝廷。

translations.literal: When Jing Su was executed his attendants scattered; Siyuan personally saw to the encoffining and burial, with his own hands planted pines and cypresses, and together with He Changyu of Lujiang and Liu Zhen of Pei commandery memorialized the court to vindicate him; the affair moved the court.
translations.idiomatic: When Jing Su was killed his followers fled. Siyuan saw to the burial, planted pines and cypresses with his own hands, and with He Changyu and Liu Zhen petitioned to clear his name. The court was moved.

sentences.zh: 景素女廢為庶人，思遠分衣食以相資贍。

translations.literal: Jing Su's daughter was degraded to commoner; Siyuan divided clothing and food to support and sustain her.
translations.idiomatic: Jing Su's daughter was reduced to commoner status. Siyuan shared food and clothing to sustain her.

sentences.zh: 年長，為備笄總，訪求素對，傾家送遣。

translations.literal: When she grew older he prepared hairpins and gathered hair, sought a plain match, and emptied the family fortune to send her away in marriage.
translations.idiomatic: When she came of age he prepared her hairpins, found a suitable husband, and spent the family fortune on her marriage.

sentences.zh: 齊建元初，曆竟陵王司徒錄事參軍、太子中舍人。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan under Qi he successively served as Recording Aide to the Prince of Jingling and Minister of Education and Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Jianyuan under Qi he served as recording aide to the Prince of Jingling and attendant of the heir apparent.

sentences.zh: 文惠太子與竟陵王子良素好士，並蒙賞接。

translations.literal: Crown Prince Wen Hui and Prince of Jingling Ziliang from of old loved scholars and both received him with favor and connection.
translations.idiomatic: Crown Prince Wen Hui and Prince Ziliang of Jingling both loved scholars and welcomed him warmly.

sentences.zh: 思遠求出為遠郡，除建安內史。

translations.literal: Siyuan requested going out to a distant commandery and was appointed Internal Administrator of Jian'an.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan asked for a distant post and was made internal administrator of Jian'an.

sentences.zh: 長兄思玄卒，思遠友于甚至，表乞自解，不許。

translations.literal: When his elder brother Sixuan died Siyuan's brotherly affection reached the utmost; he memorialized requesting self-removal and was not permitted.
translations.idiomatic: When his elder brother Sixuan died, Siyuan's devotion as a brother was extreme. He petitioned to resign and was refused.

sentences.zh: 及祥日又固陳，武帝乃許之。

translations.literal: When the day of ending mourning arrived he again firmly stated it; Emperor Wu thereupon permitted it.
translations.idiomatic: When the mourning period ended he petitioned again, and Emperor Wu allowed him to leave office.

sentences.zh: 仍除中書郎、大司馬諮議。

translations.literal: He was then appointed Director of the Secretariat and Advisory Aide to the Grand Marshal.
translations.idiomatic: He was then made director of the secretariat and advisory aide to the grand marshal.

sentences.zh: 詔舉士，竟陵王子良薦思遠及吳郡顧暠之、陳郡殷叡。

translations.literal: When the edict summoned scholars, Prince of Jingling Ziliang recommended Siyuan together with Gu Haozhi of Wu commandery and Yin Rui of Chen commandery.
translations.idiomatic: When the court sought scholars, Prince Ziliang recommended Siyuan together with Gu Haozhi of Wu and Yin Rui of Chen.

sentences.zh: 時邵陵王子貞為吳郡，除思遠為吳郡丞，以本官行郡事，論者以為得人。

translations.literal: At the time Prince of Shaoling Zizhen was Administrator of Wu commandery; Siyuan was appointed Deputy Administrator of Wu commandery and with his original office handled commandery affairs; discussers thought the right man had been obtained.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Zizhen of Shaoling governed Wu commandery and made Siyuan deputy administrator with full authority. Observers said the right man had been chosen.

sentences.zh: 後拜御史中丞。

translations.literal: Later he was appointed Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: He later became imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 臨海太守沈昭略贓私，思遠依事劾奏，明帝及思遠從兄晏、昭略叔父文季並請止之，思遠不從，案事如故。

translations.literal: Administrator of Linhai Shen Zhaolue was corrupt for private gain; Siyuan according to the matter impeached and memorialized; Emperor Ming and Siyuan's elder cousin Yan and Zhaolue's uncle by marriage Wen Ji all requested he stop, but Siyuan did not follow and investigated the affair as before.
translations.idiomatic: Linhai administrator Shen Zhaolue was corrupt. Siyuan impeached him. Emperor Ming, Siyuan's cousin Yan, and Zhaolue's uncle Wen Ji all asked him to stop. He refused and pursued the case.

sentences.zh: 建武中，遷吏部郎。

translations.literal: In Jianwu he was transferred to Director of the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: In the Jianwu era he was transferred to director of the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 思遠以晏為尚書令，不欲並居內台權要之職，上表固讓，乃改授司徒左長史。

translations.literal: Siyuan because Yan was Director of the Masters of Writing did not wish to together occupy the inner platform's weighty posts and memorialized firmly declining; he was then reassigned Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education.
translations.idiomatic: Because Yan was director of the Masters of Writing, Siyuan declined to share power on the inner platform and was reassigned as left chief administrator of the minister of education.

sentences.zh: 初明帝廢立之際，思遠謂晏曰：「兄荷武帝厚恩，今一旦贊人如此事，彼或可以權計相須，未知兄將何以自立。

translations.literal: At the beginning when Emperor Ming plotted deposition and installation Siyuan said to Yan, "Elder brother, you bear Emperor Wu's thick favor; now in one morning you assist others in such an affair—they perhaps can use expedient plans to need you, yet I do not know how elder brother will stand on his own.
translations.idiomatic: When Ming plotted the coup Siyuan told Yan: "Brother, Emperor Wu favored you deeply. Now you help others seize the throne in a morning. They may need you for now, but how will you stand afterward?

sentences.zh: 及此引決，猶可保全門戶，不失後名。

translations.literal: If at this time you resolve yourself, you can still preserve the household gates and not lose later name."
translations.idiomatic: If you end your life now, you can still save the family and your name."

sentences.zh: 」晏曰：「方噉粥，未暇此事。

translations.literal: Yan said, "Just now eating gruel; no leisure for this affair."
translations.idiomatic: Yan said: "I am eating my porridge. No time for that."

sentences.zh: 」及拜驃騎，會子弟，謂思遠兄思征曰：「隆昌之末，阿戎勸吾自裁，若用其語，豈有今日。

translations.literal: When he was appointed General of Agile Cavalry and met younger kinsmen he said to Siyuan's elder brother Sizheng, "At the end of Longchang, Arong urged me to take my own life; if I had used those words, how could there be today?"
translations.idiomatic: When he became general of agile cavalry he told Siyuan's brother Sizheng: "At the end of Longchang Arong urged me to kill myself. Had I listened, I would not be here today."

sentences.zh: 」思遠遽應曰：「如阿戎所見，猶未晚也。

translations.literal: Siyuan immediately replied, "As Arong saw it, it would still not be late."
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan answered at once: "By Arong's reckoning, it would still not be too late."

sentences.zh: 」晏既不能謙退，位處朝端，事多專斷，內外要職，並用門生，帝外跡甚美，內相疑異。

translations.literal: Yan since he could not modestly withdraw occupied the head of court; affairs were mostly decided by him alone; inside and outside important posts all used his gate students; the emperor outwardly showed great beauty yet inwardly mutually suspected difference.
translations.idiomatic: Yan would not step back. At court he decided most matters and filled posts with his clients. The emperor smiled in public but doubted him in private.

sentences.zh: 思遠謂曰：「時事稍異，兄覺不？

translations.literal: Siyuan said to him, "Current affairs are slightly different; elder brother, do you not feel it?
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan said: "Things are changing. Brother, do you not see it?

sentences.zh: 凡人多拙於自謀，而巧於謀人。

translations.literal: Most men are clumsy at plotting for themselves yet clever at plotting against others."
translations.idiomatic: Most men are clumsy at saving themselves and clever at ruining others."

sentences.zh: 」晏默然不答。

translations.literal: Yan silently did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Yan said nothing.

sentences.zh: 思遠退後，晏方歎曰：「天下人遂勸人自殺。
