translations.literal: After Siyuan withdrew Yan then sighed and said, "Men under Heaven then urge men to kill themselves."
translations.idiomatic: After Siyuan left, Yan sighed: "The whole world wants me dead."

sentences.zh: 」旬日，晏及禍。

translations.literal: Within ten days Yan reached calamity.
translations.idiomatic: Within ten days Yan was destroyed.

sentences.zh: 明帝后知思遠有此言，謂江祏曰：「王晏早用思遠語，當不至此。」

translations.literal: Afterward Emperor Ming's empress knew Siyuan had this speech and said to Jiang Shi, "If Wang Yan had early used Siyuan's words, he would not have reached this."
translations.idiomatic: Later the empress learned of Siyuan's warning and told Jiang Shi: "If Wang Yan had heeded Siyuan earlier, he would not have come to this."

sentences.zh: 思遠立身簡潔，諸客有詣己者，覘知衣服垢穢，方便不前，形儀新楚，乃與促膝。

translations.literal: Siyuan in establishing his person was simple and clean; when guests came to see him, if he observed clothes filthy he conveniently did not advance; if bearing and dress were fresh and neat he then sat knee to knee with them.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan lived simply. If a visitor's clothes were dirty he would not come forward; if the man was neat he would sit knee to knee with him.

sentences.zh: 雖然，及去之後，猶令二人交帚拂其坐處。

translations.literal: Although so, after they departed he still ordered two men with crossed brooms to sweep the place where they had sat.
translations.idiomatic: Even so, after guests left he had two servants sweep the seat where they had sat.

sentences.zh: 明帝從祖弟季敞性甚豪縱，使詣思遠，令見禮度。

translations.literal: Emperor Ming's younger cousin once removed Jichang's nature was very arrogant and unrestrained; he was sent to visit Siyuan to let him see ritual measure.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Ming's cousin Jichang was wildly arrogant. He was sent to Siyuan to learn proper conduct.

sentences.zh: 都水使者李珪之常曰：「見王思遠終日匡坐，不妄言笑，簪帽衣領，無不整潔，便憶丘明士。

translations.literal: Director of Waterways Li Guizhi often said, "Seeing Wang Siyuan sit upright all day without rash speech or laughter, hairpin, cap, collar, and clothes all without disorder, one then recalls Qiu Mingshi.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guizhi, director of waterways, often said: "See Wang Siyuan sit upright all day, never careless in speech or dress, and you think of Qiu Mingshi.

sentences.zh: 見明士蓬頭散帶，終日酣醉，吐論從橫，唐突卿宰，便復憶見思遠。

translations.literal: See Mingshi with disheveled head and loosened belt, drunk all day, spitting discourse crisscross, rudely offending ministers and administrators, and one again recalls seeing Siyuan."
translations.idiomatic: See Mingshi with hair loose and belt undone, drunk all day, talking wildly and offending ministers, and you think again of Siyuan."

sentences.zh: 」言其兩反也。

translations.literal: He spoke of their two reversals.
translations.idiomatic: He meant how opposite the two men were.

sentences.zh: 上既誅晏，思遠遷為侍中，掌優策及起居注。

translations.literal: After the emperor executed Yan, Siyuan was transferred to Attendant-in-Ordinary and managed superior policy and the record of the emperor's movements.
translations.idiomatic: After Yan's execution Siyuan became attendant-in-ordinary and oversaw court policy and the daily record.

sentences.zh: 卒，年四十九，贈太常，諡曰貞子。

translations.literal: He died, aged forty-nine, posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies, posthumous title Zhenzi.
translations.idiomatic: He died at forty-nine, was posthumously made minister of ceremonies, and titled Zhenzi.

sentences.zh: 思遠與顧暠之善，暠之卒後，家貧，思遠迎其妻子，經恤甚至。

translations.literal: Siyuan was friendly with Gu Haozhi; after Haozhi died his family was poor and Siyuan received his wife and children, sustaining them to the utmost.
translations.idiomatic: Siyuan was close to Gu Haozhi. After Haozhi died poor, Siyuan took in his wife and children and cared for them devotedly.

sentences.zh: 暠之字士明，少孤好學，有義信，位太子中舍人，兼尚書左丞。

translations.literal: Haozhi, styled Shiming, from youth was orphaned and loved learning, had righteousness and trustworthiness, and held the posts of Attendant of the Heir Apparent and concurrently Left Director of the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: Haozhi, styled Shiming, was orphaned young, loved learning, and was known for integrity. He served as attendant of the heir apparent and left director of the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 王韶之字休泰，胡之從孫而敬弘從祖弟也。

translations.literal: Wang Shaozhi, styled Xiutai, was the grandnephew of Hu Zhi and the younger cousin once removed of Jinghong.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Shaozhi, styled Xiutai, was grandnephew of Hu Zhi and a cousin once removed of Jinghong.

sentences.zh: 祖羨之，鎮軍掾。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Xianzhi, Aide to the General Who Guards the Army.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xianzhi had been aide to the general who guards the army.

sentences.zh: 父偉之，少有志尚，當世詔命表奏，輒手自書寫。

translations.literal: His father Weizhi from youth had resolve and aspiration; whenever the age's edicts, orders, memorials, and reports came forth he always with his own hand wrote them.
translations.idiomatic: His father Weizhi was ambitious from youth and copied every edict, order, and memorial by hand.

sentences.zh: 太元、隆安時事，大小悉撰錄。

translations.literal: Affairs of the Taiyuan and Long'an eras, great and small, he all compiled and recorded.
translations.idiomatic: He compiled and recorded affairs great and small from the Taiyuan and Long'an eras.

sentences.zh: 位本國郎中令。

translations.literal: He held the post of Director of the Principality in his native commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He served as director of the principality in his native commandery.

sentences.zh: 韶之家貧好學，嘗三日絕糧而執卷不輟，家人誚之曰：「困窮如此，何不耕？

translations.literal: Shaozhi's family was poor and he loved learning; once for three days he had no grain yet held the scroll without stopping; family members mocked him, saying, "So trapped in poverty—why not plow?"
translations.idiomatic: Shaozhi was poor and loved books. Once he went three days without food yet never put down his scroll. His family mocked him: "This poor—why not farm?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「我常自耕耳。

translations.literal: He replied, "I constantly plow for myself."
translations.idiomatic: He answered: "I am already farming—inside my books."

sentences.zh: 」父偉之為烏程令，韶之因居縣境。

translations.literal: His father Weizhi was Magistrate of Wucheng; Shaozhi therefore dwelt within the county border.
translations.idiomatic: His father Weizhi was magistrate of Wucheng, and Shaozhi lived within that county.

sentences.zh: 好史籍，博涉多聞。

translations.literal: He loved historical records and broadly ranged through many hearings.
translations.idiomatic: He loved history and read widely.

sentences.zh: 初為衛將軍謝琰行參軍，得父舊書，因私撰晉安帝陽秋。

translations.literal: At first he served as Acting Aide to General of the Guard Xie Yan and obtained his father's old books; therefore he privately compiled the Annals of Emperor An of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: He first served as acting aide to General Xie Yan, inherited his father's papers, and privately compiled the Annals of Emperor An of Jin.

sentences.zh: 及成，時人謂宜居史職，即除著作佐郎，使續後事，訖義熙九年。

translations.literal: When it was completed people of the time said he ought to occupy the post of historian; he was immediately appointed Assistant Gentleman of the Compilation Bureau and sent to continue later affairs, down to the ninth year of Yixi.
translations.idiomatic: When it was finished men said he should be a court historian. He was made assistant gentleman of the compilation bureau and continued the chronicle through Yixi year 9.

sentences.zh: 善敘事，辭論可觀。

translations.literal: He was skilled at narrating affairs; his discourse and argument were worth viewing.
translations.idiomatic: He narrated events well and wrote with force.

sentences.zh: 遷尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: He was transferred to gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in the Masters of Writing.

sentences.zh: 子曄，位臨賀太守。

translations.literal: His son Ye held the post of Administrator of Linhe.
translations.idiomatic: His son Ye became administrator of Linhe.

sentences.zh: 王悅之字少明，晉右軍將軍羲之曾孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Yuezhi, styled Shaoming, was the great-grandson of Jin General of the Right Army Xizhi.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Yuezhi, styled Shaoming, was great-grandson of Jin general of the right army Xizhi.

sentences.zh: 祖獻之，中書令。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Xianzhi, Director of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Xianzhi had been director of the secretariat.

sentences.zh: 父靖之，司徒左長史，為劉穆之所厚，就穆之求侍中，如此非一。

translations.literal: His father Jingzhi was Left Chief Administrator of the Minister of Education; Liu Muzhi deeply favored him; he went to Muzhi requesting Attendant-in-Ordinary, thus not once only.
translations.idiomatic: His father Jingzhi was left chief administrator of the minister of education. Liu Muzhi favored him, and Jingzhi asked Muzhi repeatedly for attendant-in-ordinary.

sentences.zh: 穆之曰：「卿若不求，久自得之。

translations.literal: Muzhi said, "If you do not request, in time you will obtain it yourself."
translations.idiomatic: Muzhi said: "If you stop asking, the post will come to you in time."

sentences.zh: 」遂不果。

translations.literal: Thereupon it did not come to pass.
translations.idiomatic: It never came.

sentences.zh: 悅之少厲清操，亮直有風檢。

translations.literal: Yuezhi from youth cultivated pure conduct and was bright, straight, and with wind and measure.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Yuezhi cultivated integrity and was upright and principled.

sentences.zh: 為吏部郎，鄰省有會同者，遺悅之餅一甌。

translations.literal: He served as Director of the Ministry of Personnel; a neighboring office had a joint meeting and sent Yuezhi one bowl of cakes.
translations.idiomatic: As director of the Ministry of Personnel he received a bowl of cakes from a neighboring office holding a joint meeting.

sentences.zh: 辭不受，曰：「此費誠小，然少來不願當之。

translations.literal: He declined and did not accept, saying, "This expense is truly small, yet from youth I have been unwilling to receive such."
translations.idiomatic: He refused them: "The gift is small, but I have never accepted such things."

sentences.zh: 」宋明帝泰始中為黃門郎、御史中丞。

translations.literal: In the Taishi era of Emperor Ming of Song he served as Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taishi era under Emperor Ming he served as attendant at the yellow gate and imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 上以其廉介，賜良田五頃，以為侍中，在門下盡其心力。

translations.literal: The emperor because of his integrity and uprightness granted five qing of fine fields and made him Attendant-in-Ordinary; in the Gate Office he exhausted his heart and strength.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rewarded his integrity with five qing of good land and made him attendant-in-ordinary. In the gate office he gave all his strength.

sentences.zh: 掌檢校禦府太官太醫諸署。

translations.literal: He managed inspection of the imperial storehouse, grand commissary, grand physician, and various offices.
translations.idiomatic: He oversaw inspection of the imperial storehouse, grand commissary, grand physician, and other offices.

sentences.zh: 時承奢忲之後，奸竊者眾，悅之按覆無所避，得奸巧甚多，於是眾署共咒詛。

translations.literal: At the time following extravagant excess, those who stole by trickery were many; Yuezhi investigated and overturned without avoidance and obtained many crafty tricksters; therefore the multitude of offices together cursed him.
translations.idiomatic: After an age of extravagance, theft was rampant. Yuezhi investigated fearlessly and exposed many frauds. The offices cursed him together.

sentences.zh: 悅之病甚，恒見兩烏衣人捶之。

translations.literal: Yuezhi's illness was severe; he constantly saw two men in black clothes beating him.
translations.idiomatic: Yuezhi fell gravely ill and constantly saw two men in black beating him.

sentences.zh: 及卒，上乃收典掌者十許人，桎梏之送淮陰，密令度瓜步江，投之中流。

translations.literal: When he died the emperor then seized about ten men who managed the records, fettered them and sent them to Huaiyin, secretly ordered measuring at Guadu crossing the river, and cast them into midstream.
translations.idiomatic: When he died the emperor seized some ten record keepers, chained them, sent them to Huaiyin, and secretly had them thrown into the Yangzi at Guadu.

sentences.zh: 王准之字元魯，晉尚書僕射彬玄孫也。

translations.literal: Wang Zhunzhi, styled Yuanlu, was the great-great-grandson of Jin Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Bin.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Zhunzhi, styled Yuanlu, was great-great-grandson of Jin Vice Director Bin.

sentences.zh: 曾祖彪之，位尚書令，祖臨之、父訥之並御史中丞。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather was Biaozhi, who held the post of Director of the Masters of Writing; his grandfather Linzhi and father Nezhi both served as Imperial Censor.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Biaozhi had been director of the Masters of Writing; his grandfather Linzhi and father Nezhi both served as imperial censor.

sentences.zh: 彪之博聞多識，練悉朝儀，自是家世相傳，並諳江左舊事，緘之青箱，世謂之王氏青箱學。

translations.literal: Biaozhi was broad in hearing and many in knowledge, skilled and familiar with court ceremony; from this the family transmitted generation after generation, all versed in old affairs east of the Yangzi, sealed in the blue box; the age called it the Wang clan's Blue Box Learning.
translations.idiomatic: Biaozhi knew court ritual thoroughly, and the family preserved Jiangdong precedent in their blue chests for generations. Men called it the Wang clan's Blue Box Learning.

sentences.zh: 准之兼明禮傳，贍于文辭。

translations.literal: Zhunzhi was also clear in the Rites and Commentary and rich in literary phrasing.
translations.idiomatic: Zhunzhi also mastered the Rites and wrote with ease.

sentences.zh: 桓玄篡位，以為尚書祠部郎。

translations.literal: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne he was made Gentleman of the Ministry of Rites in the Masters of Writing.
translations.idiomatic: When Huan Xuan usurped the throne Zhunzhi was made gentleman of the Ministry of Rites.

sentences.zh: 宋武帝起兵，為太尉主簿。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Song raised armies he served as Chief Clerk to the Grand Commandant.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu raised his armies Zhunzhi served as chief clerk to the grand commandant.

sentences.zh: 出為山陰令，有能名，預討盧循功，封都亭侯。

translations.literal: He went out as Magistrate of Shanyin and had reputation for ability; he shared in the achievement of campaigning against Lu Xun and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Duting.
translations.idiomatic: As magistrate of Shanyin he earned a name for competence, shared in the campaign against Lu Xun, and was enfeoffed as marquis of Duting.

sentences.zh: 宋台建，除御史中丞，為百僚所憚。

translations.literal: When the Song Platform was established he was appointed Imperial Censor and was feared by the hundred officials.
translations.idiomatic: When the Song platform was formed he became imperial censor and was feared throughout the bureaucracy.

sentences.zh: 自彪之至准之四世居此職。

translations.literal: From Biaozhi to Zhunzhi four generations occupied this post.
translations.idiomatic: From Biaozhi to Zhunzhi four generations held that office.

sentences.zh: 准之嘗作五言詩，範泰嘲之：「卿唯解彈事耳。

translations.literal: Zhunzhi once composed a five-character poem; Fan Tai mocked him: "You only understand impeachment affairs."
translations.idiomatic: Zhunzhi once wrote a five-character poem. Fan Tai mocked him: "All you know is filing impeachments."

sentences.zh: 」准之正色答：「猶差卿世載雄狐。

translations.literal: Zhunzhi with stern countenance replied, "Still better than your family for generations loading male foxes."
translations.idiomatic: Zhunzhi answered coldly: "Still better than your family, which for generations has bred male foxes."

sentences.zh: 」坐世子左衛率謝靈運殺人不舉，免官。

translations.literal: Because the Heir Apparent's Left Leader of Guard Xie Lingyun killed a man and did not report it, he was removed from office.
translations.idiomatic: He was dismissed because Xie Lingyun, left leader of guard to the heir apparent, had killed a man without reporting it.

sentences.zh: 武帝受命，拜黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu received the Mandate he was appointed Attendant at the Yellow Gate.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu received the mandate Zhunzhi was appointed attendant at the yellow gate.

sentences.zh: 永初中奏曰：「鄭玄注禮：三年之喪，二十七月而吉。

translations.literal: In the beginning of Yongchu he memorialized, saying, "Zheng Xuan annotated the Rites: three years of mourning, in the twenty-seventh month one reaches auspiciousness.
translations.idiomatic: Early in Yongchu he memorialized: "Zheng Xuan's commentary on the Rites holds that three years of mourning end in auspiciousness in the twenty-seventh month.

sentences.zh: 古今學者多謂得禮之宜。

translations.literal: Scholars ancient and modern mostly say this obtains the Rites' appropriateness.
translations.idiomatic: Scholars ancient and modern mostly say this accords with the Rites.

sentences.zh: 晉初用王肅議，祥禫共月，故二十五月而除。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Jin they used Wang Su's deliberation; end-of-mourning and sacrificial repose shared a month, therefore in the twenty-fifth month mourning was removed.
translations.idiomatic: Early Jin followed Wang Su's view, combining end-of-mourning and sacrificial repose in one month, so mourning ended in the twenty-fifth month.

sentences.zh: 遂以為制。

translations.literal: Thereupon it was taken as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: That became the rule.

sentences.zh: 江左以來，唯晉朝施用，搢紳之士多遵玄義。

translations.literal: East of the Yangzi since then only the Jin court applied it; gentry scholars mostly followed Xuan's meaning.
translations.idiomatic: Since then only the Jin court used it east of the Yangzi, though many gentry followed Zheng Xuan's interpretation.

sentences.zh: 夫先王制禮，以大順群心，'喪也甯戚'，著自前經。

translations.literal: The former kings made rites to accord with great compliance with the multitude's hearts; 'In mourning, better give way to grief' is shown from former classics.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient kings fashioned rites to align with men's hearts: 'In mourning, let grief prevail,' as the classics teach.

sentences.zh: 今大宋開泰，品物遂理，愚謂宜同即物情，以玄義為制。

translations.literal: Now Great Song opens peace, all things follow order; I foolishly propose it ought to follow present human feeling and take Xuan's meaning as regulation.
translations.idiomatic: Now that Song brings order to the realm, I propose we follow present sentiment and adopt Zheng Xuan's rule.

sentences.zh: 朝野一禮，則家無殊俗。

translations.literal: Court and countryside one rite, then households have no different customs."
translations.idiomatic: One rite for court and country, and no household will mourn differently."

sentences.zh: 」從之。

translations.literal: The emperor followed it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor agreed.

sentences.zh: 元嘉中，歷位侍中，都官尚書，改領吏部，出為丹陽尹。

translations.literal: In the Yuanjia era he successively served as Attendant-in-Ordinary, Director of the Ministry of Punishments, was changed to concurrently Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and went out as Intendant of Danyang.
translations.idiomatic: In the Yuanjia era he served as attendant-in-ordinary, director of the Ministry of Punishments, then director of the Ministry of Personnel, and finally intendant of Danyang.

sentences.zh: 准之究識舊儀，問無不對。

translations.literal: Zhunzhi thoroughly knew old ceremonies; asked, there was nothing he did not answer.
translations.idiomatic: Zhunzhi knew old ceremony inside out and could answer any question.

sentences.zh: 時大將軍彭城王義康錄尚書事，每歎曰：「何須高論玄虛，正得如王准之兩三人，天下便足。

translations.literal: At the time Grand General Prince of Pengcheng Yikang recorded affairs of the Masters of Writing; each time he sighed and said, "Why need high discourse on mystery and emptiness? Just obtaining two or three men like Wang Zhunzhi, all under Heaven is sufficient."
translations.idiomatic: Grand General Yikang, Prince of Pengcheng, who oversaw the Masters of Writing, often sighed: "Why talk mysticism? Two or three men like Wang Zhunzhi would be enough for the realm."

sentences.zh: 」然寡風素，情悁急，不為時流所重。

translations.literal: Yet he lacked wind and plainness; his temperament was narrow and urgent and he was not heavily regarded by the currents of the age.
translations.idiomatic: Yet he lacked easy grace; impatient by nature, he was not widely admired.

sentences.zh: 撰儀注，咸見遵用。

translations.literal: He compiled ceremonial regulations; all were seen and followed in use.
translations.idiomatic: His ceremonial compilations were all adopted.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太常。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously made minister of ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 子輿之，征虜主簿。

translations.literal: His son was Yuzhi, Chief Clerk to the General Who Conquers the Barbarians.
translations.idiomatic: His son Yuzhi served as chief clerk to the general who conquers the barbarians.

sentences.zh: 輿之子進之，仕齊位給事黃門侍郎，扶風太守。

translations.literal: Yuzhi's son was Jinzhi; he served Qi as Attendant at the Yellow Gate and Director of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Fufeng, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: Yuzhi's son Jinzhi served Qi as attendant at the yellow gate, director of the Masters of Writing, and administrator of Fufeng, and was enfeoffed as duke of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 梁武帝之舉兵也，所在回應，鄰郡多請進之同遣修謁。

translations.literal: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised armies, everywhere responded; neighboring commanderies mostly requested Jinzhi together dispatch envoys to pay court.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Wu of Liang raised his armies the region rallied. Neighboring commanderies asked Jinzhi to join them in sending envoys to submit.

sentences.zh: 進之曰：「非吾志也。

translations.literal: Jinzhi said, "This is not my will."
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhi said: "That is not my wish."

sentences.zh: 」竟不行。

translations.literal: In the end he did not go.
translations.idiomatic: He never went.

sentences.zh: 武帝嘉之。

translations.literal: Emperor Wu praised this.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wu praised his restraint.

sentences.zh: 梁台建，曆尚書左丞，廣平、天門二郡太守，左衛將軍，封建甯公。

translations.literal: When the Liang Platform was established he successively served as Left Director of the Masters of Writing, Administrator of Guangping and Tianmen, Left Leader of the Guard, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Jianning.
translations.idiomatic: When the Liang platform was formed he served as left director of the Masters of Writing, administrator of Guangping and Tianmen, left leader of the guard, and was enfeoffed as duke of Jianning.

sentences.zh: 進之子清，位散騎常侍，金紫光祿大夫，鎮東府長史，新野、東陽二郡太守，安南將軍，封中廬公。

translations.literal: Jinzhi's son Qing held the posts of Supernumerary Regular Attendant, Grand Master of the Bright Hall with Golden Tassel, Chief Administrator of the Eastern Palace, Administrator of Xinye and Dongyang, General Who Pacifies the South, and was enfeoffed as Duke of Zhonglu.
translations.idiomatic: Jinzhi's son Qing served as supernumerary regular attendant, grand master of the bright hall with golden tassel, chief administrator of the eastern palace, administrator of Xinye and Dongyang, general who pacifies the south, and was enfeoffed as duke of Zhonglu.

sentences.zh: 承聖末，陳武帝殺太尉王僧辯，遣文帝攻僧辯婿杜龕，龕告難於清，引兵援龕，大敗陳文帝于吳興，追奔至晉陵。

translations.literal: At the end of Chengsheng Emperor Wu of Chen killed Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian and sent Emperor Wen to attack Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan; Kan reported distress to Qing and led troops to aid Kan; he greatly defeated Emperor Wen at Wuxing and pursued the rout to Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Chengsheng, Chen Emperor Wu killed Grand Commandant Wang Sengbian and sent Emperor Wen against Sengbian's son-in-law Du Kan. Kan appealed to Qing, who marched to his aid and routed Emperor Wen at Wuxing, pursuing him to Jinling.

sentences.zh: 時廣州刺史歐陽頠亦同清援龕，中更改異，殺清而歸陳武帝。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector of Guangzhou Ouyang Wei also together with Qing aided Kan; midway he changed and differed, killed Qing and returned to Emperor Wu of Chen.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Ouyang Wei had also joined Qing to aid Kan, but midway he turned, killed Qing, and submitted to Chen Emperor Wu.

sentences.zh: 子猛。

translations.literal: His son was Meng.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Meng.

sentences.zh: 猛字世雄，本名勇。

translations.literal: Meng, styled Shixiong, original name Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Meng, styled Shixiong, was originally named Yong.

sentences.zh: 五歲而父清遇害，陳文帝軍度浙江，訪之，將加夷滅。

translations.literal: When he was five his father Qing met with calamity; when Emperor Wen's army crossed the Zhe River they sought him and were about to exterminate the clan.
translations.idiomatic: When he was five his father Qing was killed. As Emperor Wen's army crossed the Zhe they searched for the family to exterminate them.

sentences.zh: 母韋氏攜之遁於會稽，遂免。

translations.literal: His mother Lady Wei carried him in flight to Kuaiji and therefore escaped.
translations.idiomatic: His mother Lady Wei fled with him to Kuaiji and he survived.

sentences.zh: 及長勤學不倦，博涉經史，兼習孫、吳兵法。

translations.literal: When he grew older he diligently studied without tiring, broadly ranged through classics and histories, and concurrently studied the military methods of Sun and Wu.
translations.idiomatic: As he grew he studied tirelessly, mastered the classics and histories, and also learned the art of war of Sun and Wu.

sentences.zh: 以父遇酷，終文帝之世不聽音樂，蔬食布衣，以喪禮自處。

translations.literal: Because his father met with harsh treatment, through Emperor Wen's age he did not listen to music, ate vegetables and wore plain cloth, and treated himself with mourning rites.
translations.idiomatic: Because his father had been killed unjustly, he refused music throughout Emperor Wen's reign, ate plainly, wore hemp, and lived as if in mourning.

sentences.zh: 宣帝立，乃始求位。

translations.literal: When Emperor Xuan established himself he then began to seek office.
translations.idiomatic: Only when Emperor Xuan took the throne did he seek office.

sentences.zh: 太建初，釋褐鄱陽王府中兵參軍，再遷永陽王府錄事參軍。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Taijian he doffed plain cloth as Military Aide in the Prince of Poyang's headquarters, was again transferred to Recording Aide in the Prince of Yongyang's headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Taijian he entered service as military aide on the Prince of Poyang's staff, then became recording aide on the Prince of Yongyang's staff.

sentences.zh: 猛慷慨常慕功名，先是上疏陳安邊拓境之策，甚見嘉納，至是詔隨大都督吳明徹略地，以軍功封應陽縣子。

translations.literal: Meng was generous and often admired achievement and fame; earlier he had memorialized strategies for securing the border and expanding territory and was greatly praised and accepted; at this time an edict ordered him to follow the Grand Commander Wu Mingche in seizing territory; because of military achievement he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Yingyang.
translations.idiomatic: Meng was bold and hungered for glory. He had earlier submitted plans to secure the frontier and was praised. Now he followed Grand Commander Wu Mingche on campaign and was enfeoffed as viscount of Yingyang for his service.

sentences.zh: 累遷太子右衛率，徙晉陵太守。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Right Leader of Guard for the Heir Apparent and transferred to Administrator of Jinling.
translations.idiomatic: He rose to right leader of guard for the heir apparent and was transferred to administrator of Jinling.

sentences.zh: 威惠兼舉，奸盜屏跡，富商野次，云：「以付王府君」。

translations.literal: Authority and kindness were both raised; thieves and robbers vanished from sight; rich merchants in the wild said, "Entrust it to the prince's lord."
translations.idiomatic: He combined sternness with mercy until bandits disappeared. Merchants on the roads said: "Leave it to the prince's governor."

sentences.zh: 郡人歌之，以比漢之趙廣漢。

translations.literal: People of the commandery sang of him and compared him to Zhao Guanghan of Han.
translations.idiomatic: The people sang of him and compared him to Han's Zhao Guanghan.

sentences.zh: 至德初，徵為左驍騎將軍，加散騎常侍，深見信重。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Zhide he was summoned as General of the Left Agile Cavalry with additional rank as Supernumerary Regular Attendant and was deeply trusted.
translations.idiomatic: At the start of Zhide he was summoned as general of the left agile cavalry with supernumerary regular attendant and was deeply trusted.

sentences.zh: 時孔范、施文慶等並相與比周，害其梗直，議將出之而未有便。

translations.literal: At the time Kong Fan, Shi Wenqing, and others all associated in factions; they harmed his upright sternness and plotted to send him out yet had no convenient occasion.
translations.idiomatic: Kong Fan, Shi Wenqing, and others formed factions, resented his blunt integrity, and wanted to banish him but found no occasion.

sentences.zh: 會廣州刺史馬靖不受征，乃除猛都督東衡州刺史，領始興內史，與廣州刺史陳方慶共取靖。

translations.literal: It happened that Inspector of Guangzhou Ma Jing did not accept summons; thereupon Meng was appointed Commander of East Hengzhou, concurrently Internal Administrator of Shixing, and together with Inspector of Guangzhou Chen Fangqing seized Jing.
translations.idiomatic: When Guangzhou inspector Ma Jing refused summons, Meng was made commander of East Hengzhou and internal administrator of Shixing, and with Guangzhou inspector Chen Fangqing took Jing.

sentences.zh: 猛至，即禽靖送建鄴，進爵為公，加光勝將軍、平越中郎將、大都督，發廣、桂等二十州兵討嶺外荒梗，所至皆平。

translations.literal: When Meng arrived he at once captured Jing and sent him to Jiankang; he advanced in rank to duke, was given additional title General of Luminous Victory and General of the Army Who Pacifies the Yue, Grand Commander, and dispatched troops of twenty commanderies including Guang and Gui to campaign against uncivilized regions beyond the ranges; wherever he reached all was pacified.
translations.idiomatic: Meng captured Jing at once and sent him to Jiankang. He was raised to duke, given the titles general of luminous victory and general of the army who pacifies the Yue, and sent with troops from twenty commanderies to pacify the far south. Wherever he went, order followed.

sentences.zh: 禎明二年，詔授鎮南大將軍、都督二十四州諸軍事，尋命徙鎮廣州。

translations.literal: In the second year of Zhenming an edict appointed him General Who Guards the South and Commander of twenty-four provinces' military affairs; soon he was ordered transferred to garrison Guangzhou.
translations.idiomatic: In Zhenming year 2 he was made general who guards the south and commander of twenty-four provinces. Soon he was ordered to transfer his garrison to Guangzhou.

sentences.zh: 未之鎮，而隋師濟江，猛總督所部赴援。

translations.literal: Before he reached the garrison Sui armies crossed the river; Meng overall commanded his command and went to aid.
translations.idiomatic: Before he took up the post Sui armies crossed the Yangzi. Meng led his forces to the rescue.

sentences.zh: 時廣州刺史臨汝侯方慶、西衡州刺史衡陽王伯信並隸猛督府，各觀望不至。

translations.literal: At the time Inspector of Guangzhou the Marquis of Linru Fangqing and Inspector of West Hengzhou the Prince of Hengyang Boxin both were under Meng's command headquarters; each watched and did not arrive.
translations.idiomatic: Guangzhou inspector Fangqing, Marquis of Linru, and West Hengzhou inspector Prince Boxin of Hengyang were under his command but held back and never came.

sentences.zh: 猛使高州刺史戴智烈、清遠太守曾孝遠各以輕兵就斬之而發其兵。

translations.literal: Meng sent Administrator of Gaozhou Dai Zhilie and Administrator of Qingyuan Zeng Xiaoyuan each with light troops to go and behead them and then mobilize their armies.
translations.idiomatic: Meng sent Dai Zhilie, administrator of Gaozhou, and Zeng Xiaoyuan, administrator of Qingyuan, each with light troops to execute them and seize their armies.

sentences.zh: 及聞台城不守，乃舉哀素服，藉稿不食，歎曰：「申包胥獨何人哉。

translations.literal: When he heard the capital could not be held he then raised mourning in plain garments, spread straw and did not eat, sighed and said, "Was Shen Baoxu alone a man?"
translations.idiomatic: When he learned the capital had fallen he put on mourning, lay on straw, and refused food, sighing: "Was Shen Baoxu the only man who could do this?"

sentences.zh: 」因勒兵緣江拒守，以固誠節。

translations.literal: Thereupon he marshaled troops along the river to resist and guard and thereby fixed loyal integrity.
translations.idiomatic: He then marshaled troops along the river to hold the line and keep faith with the fallen dynasty.

sentences.zh: 及審後主不死，乃遣其部將辛昉馳驛赴京師歸款。

translations.literal: When he verified the Later Lord had not died he then sent his subordinate general Xin Fang galloping by post relay to the capital to submit allegiance.
translations.idiomatic: Learning the later lord still lived, he sent his officer Xin Fang by post relay to the capital to offer submission.

sentences.zh: 隋文帝大悅，謂昉曰：「猛懷其舊主，送故情深，即是我之誠臣。

translations.literal: Emperor Wen of Sui greatly delighted and said to Fang, "Meng cherishes his old lord and sends off the former ruler with deep feeling—he is at once my loyal minister.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Wen of Sui was delighted and told Fang: "Meng keeps faith with his old master and sees the former ruler off with true feeling. That makes him my loyal minister.

sentences.zh: 保守一方，不勞兵甲，又是我之功臣。

translations.literal: Guarding one region without troubling soldiers and armor—he is also my meritorious minister."
translations.idiomatic: He holds a region without forcing me to send armies. That makes him my meritorious minister too."

sentences.zh: 」即日拜昉開府儀同三司，仍詔猛與行軍總管韋洸便留嶺表經略。

translations.literal: That same day Fang was appointed Grand Master with Golden Tally Equal in Ceremony to the Three Excellencies; still an edict ordered Meng together with Campaign Commander Wei Guang to remain in Lingbiao and manage strategy.
translations.idiomatic: That day Fang was made grand master with golden tally equal in ceremony to the three excellencies, and Meng was ordered with campaign commander Wei Guang to remain in Lingnan and govern the region.

sentences.zh: 逡之字宣約，少禮學博聞。

translations.literal: Qunzhi, styled Xuanyue, from youth was versed in ritual learning and broad in hearing.
translations.idiomatic: Qunzhi, styled Xuanyue, mastered ritual learning from youth and was widely read.

sentences.zh: 仕宋位吳令。

translations.literal: He served Song as Magistrate of Wu.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song he served as magistrate of Wu.

sentences.zh: 升明末，尚書右僕射王儉重儒術，逡之以著作郎兼尚書左丞，參定齊國儀禮。

translations.literal: At the end of the Shengming era Right Vice Director of the Masters of Writing Wang Jian valued Confucian learning; Qunzhi as Gentleman of the Compilation Bureau concurrently served as Left Director of the Masters of Writing and fixed Qi state's ceremonial rites.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Shengming, Vice Director Wang Jian valued Confucian learning. Qunzhi, as gentleman of the compilation bureau and left director of the Masters of Writing, helped fix Qi ceremonial rites.

sentences.zh: 初，儉撰古今喪服集記，逡之難儉十一條，更撰世行五卷。

translations.literal: At first Jian compiled a collected record of mourning garments ancient and modern; Qunzhi challenged Jian on eleven articles and separately compiled World Practice in five scrolls.
translations.idiomatic: Jian had compiled a record of mourning garments ancient and modern. Qunzhi challenged eleven of his points and wrote World Practice in five scrolls.

sentences.zh: 國學久廢，齊建元二年，逡之先上表立學。

translations.literal: The Imperial University long abandoned, in the second year of Jianyuan Qunzhi first memorialized to establish the school.
translations.idiomatic: The imperial university had long lain idle. In Jianyuan year 2 Qunzhi first petitioned to restore it.

sentences.zh: 轉國子博士，又兼著作。

translations.literal: He was transferred to Erudite of the Imperial University and also concurrently compiled.
translations.idiomatic: He became erudite of the imperial university and also served in the compilation bureau.

sentences.zh: 撰永明起居注。

translations.literal: He compiled the Yongming Record of the Emperor's Movements.
translations.idiomatic: He wrote the daily record of the Yongming reign.

sentences.zh: 後位南康相，光祿大夫，加給事中。

translations.literal: Later he held the posts of Administrator of Nankang, Grand Master of the Bright Hall, with additional rank as Supernumerary Regular Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: He later served as administrator of Nankang and grand master of the bright hall with supernumerary regular attendant.

sentences.zh: 逡之率素，衣裳不澣，几案塵黑，年老手不釋卷。

translations.literal: Qunzhi was plain in leading his person; clothes and garments were unwashed, desks and cases dust-black; in old age his hand did not release the scroll.
translations.idiomatic: Qunzhi lived plainly: unwashed clothes, black with dust on his desk, and in old age he never put down his books.

sentences.zh: 建武二年卒。

translations.literal: He died in the second year of Jianwu.
translations.idiomatic: He died in Jianwu year 2.

sentences.zh: 從弟珪之，位長水校尉，撰齊職儀。

translations.literal: His younger cousin Guizhi held the post of Commandant of the Chang Water and compiled Qi Office Regulations.
translations.idiomatic: His cousin Guizhi served as commandant of the chang water and compiled Qi Office Regulations.

sentences.zh: 永明九年，其子中軍參軍顥啟上其書，凡五十卷，詔付秘閣。

translations.literal: In the ninth year of Yongming his son Ha, a military aide in the central army, memorialized presenting his book, fifty scrolls in all; an edict delivered it to the secret vault.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongming year 9 his son Ha, a central army aide, presented the work—fifty scrolls in all—and an edict placed it in the secret vault.

sentences.zh: 素字休業，彬五世孫而逡之族子也。

translations.literal: Su, styled Xiuye, was the fifth-generation descendant of Bin and Qunzhi's clansman.
translations.idiomatic: Su, styled Xiuye, was Bin's fifth-generation descendant and Qunzhi's clansman.

sentences.zh: 高祖翹之，晉光祿大夫。

translations.literal: High Ancestor Qiaozhi was Jin Grand Master of the Bright Hall.
translations.idiomatic: His high ancestor Qiaozhi was Jin grand master of the bright hall.

sentences.zh: 曾祖望之、祖泰之，並不仕。

translations.literal: Great-grandfather Wangzhi and grandfather Taizhi both did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Wangzhi and grandfather Taizhi both refused office.

sentences.zh: 父元弘，位平固令。

translations.literal: His father Yuanhong held the post of Magistrate of Pinggu.
translations.idiomatic: His father Yuanhong was magistrate of Pinggu.

sentences.zh: 素少有志行，家貧母老，隱居不仕。

translations.literal: Su from youth had resolve and conduct; the family was poor and his mother old; he hid and dwelt and did not take office.
translations.idiomatic: Su had strong character from youth. His family was poor and his mother old, so he lived in seclusion and refused office.

sentences.zh: 宋孝建、大明、泰始中，屢征不就，聲譽甚高。

translations.literal: In Xiaojian, Daming, and Taishi under Song he was repeatedly summoned and did not go; his reputation was very high.
translations.idiomatic: Under Song in the Xiaojian, Daming, and Taishi eras he was summoned repeatedly and never came. His repute was very high.

sentences.zh: 山中有蚿聲清長，聽之使人不厭，而其形甚醜，素乃為蚿賦以自況。

translations.literal: In the mountains there was a centipede whose sound was clear and long; hearing it made men not weary, yet its form was very ugly; Su therefore composed a Centipede Rhapsody to compare himself.
translations.idiomatic: Mountain centipedes sang with a clear, lingering voice that never tired the ear, though the creature itself was ugly. Su wrote a Centipede Rhapsody comparing himself to it.

sentences.zh: 卒年五十四。

translations.literal: He died aged fifty-four.
translations.idiomatic: He died at fifty-four.

sentences.zh: 論曰：昔晉初度江，王導卜其家世，郭璞云：「淮流竭，王氏滅。

translations.literal: The discourse says: In former days at the beginning of Jin when crossing the river, Wang Dao divined his family's fate; Guo Pu said, "When the Huai River's flow is exhausted, the Wang clan is destroyed."
translations.idiomatic: The commentary says: When the Jin first crossed the Yangzi, Wang Dao asked Guo Pu to read his family's fate. Guo Pu said: "When the Huai runs dry, the Wang clan falls."

sentences.zh: 」觀夫晉氏以來，諸王冠冕不替，蓋亦人倫所得，豈唯世祿之所專乎。

translations.literal: Observing from the Jin clan since then, the various Wangs caps and emblems unbroken—this is also what human relations obtain; how is it only what generations of emolument monopolize?
translations.idiomatic: Since then the Wangs had never lost rank among the great houses. That owed something to human talent, not salary alone.

sentences.zh: 及于陳亡之年，淮流實竭，曩時人物掃地盡矣。

translations.literal: When it reached the year Chen perished, the Huai River's flow indeed was exhausted; the figures of that time were swept from the earth entirely.
translations.idiomatic: In the year Chen fell the Huai indeed ran dry, and the men of that age were swept away.

sentences.zh: 斯乃興亡之兆已有前定。

translations.literal: This then was an omen of rise and fall already fixed beforehand.
translations.idiomatic: The omen of rise and fall had been fixed long before.

sentences.zh: 天之所廢，豈智識之所謀乎。

translations.literal: What Heaven abandons—how can wisdom and knowledge plot against it?
translations.idiomatic: What Heaven casts aside—can wit or wisdom defy it?
